title.zh: 卷九十六 列傳第三十四: 黃久約 李晏子:仲略 李愈 王賁 許安仁 梁襄 路伯達
title.en: Volume 96 Biographies 34: Huang Jiuyue, Li Yan son: Zhonglüe, Li Yu, Wang Ben, Xu Anren, Liang Xiang, Lu Boda
title.raw: 卷九十六 列傳第三十四: 黃久約 李晏子:仲略 李愈 王賁 許安仁 梁襄 路伯達 Volume 96 Biographies 34: Huang Jiuyue, Li Yan son: Zhonglüe, Li Yu, Wang Ben, Xu Anren, Liang Xiang, Lu Boda

sentences.zh: 黃久約

translations.literal: Huang Jiuyue
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jiuyue

sentences.zh: 黃久約，字彌大，東平須城人也。

translations.literal: Huang Jiuyue, styled Yida, was a man of Xucheng in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jiuyue, whose courtesy name was Yida, came from Xucheng in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 曾祖孝綽有隱德，號「潛山先生」。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaochuo possessed hidden virtue and was styled "Mr. Hidden Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiaochuo was a man of quiet moral excellence, known as "Master Hidden Mountain."

sentences.zh: 父勝，通判濟州。

translations.literal: His father Sheng served as vice commissioner of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng held the post of vice commissioner in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 母劉氏，尚書右丞長言之妹，一夕夢鼠銜明珠，寤而久約生，歲實在子也。

translations.literal: His mother was the Liu clan, younger sister of the Vice Director of the Right of the Ministry of Works Liu Changyan; one night she dreamed of a mouse carrying a bright pearl, and upon waking Jiuyue was born—the year was actually the year of zi.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Liu family, was the younger sister of Liu Changyan, Vice Director of the Right in the Ministry of Works. One night she dreamed that a mouse was carrying a lustrous pearl; when she awoke, Jiuyue had been born—the birth year was indeed a zi year.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，調鄆城主簿，三遷曹州軍事判官。

translations.literal: He was advanced to jinshi rank, appointed chief clerk of Yuncheng, and after three promotions became military judge of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was posted as chief clerk in Yuncheng; after three promotions he became military judge in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 有盜竊民財，訴者以為強，郡守欲傅以重辟。

translations.literal: There was a thief who stole the people's property; the complainant treated it as robbery, and the prefect wished to apply the heavy penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When a man stole civilians' property, the plaintiff charged him with robbery, and the prefect wanted to impose the capital offense.

sentences.zh: 久約閱實，囚得免死。

translations.literal: Jiuyue examined the facts, and the prisoner was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyue reviewed the case on its merits, and the prisoner escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 累擢禮部員外郎，兼翰林修撰，升待制，授磁州刺史。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, concurrently Hanlin Compiler, was raised to Academician-in-Waiting, and was appointed Prefect of Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, served concurrently as Hanlin Compiler, was elevated to Academician-in-Waiting, and was appointed prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 磁並山，素多盜，既獲而款伏者，審錄官或不時至，系者多以杖殺，或死獄中。

translations.literal: Cizhou borders the mountains and had always had many bandits; once captives had confessed, the interrogation officials sometimes did not arrive in time, and those detained were often beaten to death or died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Cizhou lay against the mountains and had long been rife with bandits. After captives were taken and had confessed, the interrogators sometimes failed to arrive promptly; many detainees were beaten to death, or perished in jail.

sentences.zh: 久約惻然曰：「民雖為盜，而不死於法可乎？

translations.literal: Jiuyue said with compassion, "Though the people have become bandits, may they not die by the law?
translations.idiomatic: Moved to pity, Jiuyue said, "These people may have turned to robbery, but must they die under the law?

sentences.zh: 」乃盡請讞之而後行。

translations.literal: " He then had every case fully reviewed before carrying out punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " He required every case to be fully adjudicated before any sentence was carried out.

sentences.zh: 久之，複入翰林為直學士，尋授左諫議大夫，兼禮部侍郎，為賀宋生日副使。

translations.literal: After some time he re-entered the Hanlin as Academician Expositor, was soon appointed Left Remonstrance Counsellor and concurrently Vice Minister of Rites, and served as deputy envoy to congratulate the Song on the emperor's birthday.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he returned to the Hanlin as Academician Expositor, was soon made Left Remonstrance Counsellor while retaining a concurrent post as Vice Minister of Rites, and was sent as deputy envoy to offer birthday congratulations to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 至臨安，適館伴使病，宋人議欲以副使代行使事，久約曰：「設副使亦病，又將使都轄、掌儀輩行禮乎？

translations.literal: When he reached Lin'an, it happened that the escort commissioner fell ill; the Song side proposed that the deputy envoy should act in his place and conduct the ceremonies. Jiuyue said, "Suppose the deputy envoy also falls ill—will you then have commanders and protocol officers perform the rites?
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Lin'an, the Song escort commissioner happened to fall ill, and the Song officials proposed that the deputy envoy should stand in for him and conduct the ceremonies. Jiuyue objected: "If the deputy envoy falls ill as well, will you next have local commanders and protocol officers perform the rites?

sentences.zh: 」竟令國信使獨前行，副使與館伴副使聯騎如故，乃終禮而還。

translations.literal: " In the end he had the trust envoy proceed alone in the lead, while the deputy envoy rode paired with the deputy escort commissioner as before, and thus completed the ceremonies and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he had the chief trust envoy go forward alone, while he himself rode paired with the deputy escort commissioner as usual; the ceremonies were completed and the mission returned home.

sentences.zh: 道經宿、泗，見貢新枇杷子者，州縣調民夫遞進，還奏罷之。

translations.literal: Passing through Suzhou and Sizhou, he saw tribute of fresh loquats; the prefectures and counties were conscripting corvée laborers for relay transport. On his return he memorialized to abolish the practice.
translations.idiomatic: On the road through Suzhou and Sizhou he saw fresh loquats being presented as tribute, with local officials drafting corvée labor for relay transport. When he returned he memorialized to have the practice stopped.

sentences.zh: 時以貧富不均，或欲令富民分貸貧者，下有司議，久約曰：「物之不齊，物之情也。

translations.literal: At the time, because wealth and poverty were unequal, some wished to have the wealthy lend in shares to the poor; the matter was referred to the relevant offices for discussion. Jiuyue said, "That things are not equal is the nature of things.
translations.idiomatic: Because wealth and poverty were unevenly distributed, some proposed that the rich should be made to lend to the poor in shares; the matter was sent down to the ministries for deliberation. Jiuyue said, "That things are unequal is simply their nature.

sentences.zh: 貧富不均，亦理之常。

translations.literal: Unequal wealth and poverty is also the constant pattern of principle.
translations.idiomatic: Unequal distribution of wealth is likewise the ordinary course of affairs.

sentences.zh: 若從或者言，適足以斂怨，非損有餘補不足之道。

translations.literal: If we follow the words of those people, it would only suffice to gather resentment—it is not the way of taking from surplus to supplement deficiency.
translations.idiomatic: If we followed that proposal, we would only breed resentment; it is not the true way of drawing on surplus to relieve want.

sentences.zh: 」章宗時領右丞相，韙其議。

translations.literal: " At that time Zhangzong was acting as Right Chancellor and approved his view.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhangzong, who was then serving as Right Chancellor, endorsed his argument.

sentences.zh: 尋上章請老，詔諭之曰：「卿忠直敢言，匡益甚多，未可使去左右。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; an edict instructed him, saying, "You are loyal, upright, and daring in speech; your corrections and benefits have been many—you must not yet be allowed to leave Our side.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he submitted a memorial asking to retire. An edict reassured him: "You are loyal, forthright, and fearless in remonstrance, and you have done the court much good; We cannot yet let you leave Our side.

sentences.zh: 」遷太常卿，仍兼諫職。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, while still retaining his remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while keeping his remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 時郡縣多闕官，久約言：「世豈乏材，閡於資格故也。

translations.literal: At the time many prefectures and counties lacked officials. Jiuyue said, "How could the age lack talent? It is because qualification rules obstruct it.
translations.idiomatic: Many prefectures and counties were then short of officials. Jiuyue said, "The age is not short of talent; rigid qualification rules are what block it.

sentences.zh: 明詔每責大臣以守格法而滯人材，乞斷自宸衷而力行之。

translations.literal: Bright edicts repeatedly reproach the great ministers for clinging to formal regulations and thereby stalling talent; I beg that Your Majesty decide from the imperial heart and carry it out with force.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts have repeatedly rebuked the chief ministers for clinging to formal regulations and thereby stalling talent. I beg Your Majesty to decide this from your own judgment and enforce it resolutely.

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「此事宰相不屬意，而使諫臣言之歟？

translations.literal: " Shizong said, "On this matter the chancellor paid no attention, and so a remonstrance official had to speak of it?
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong said, "The chancellor paid no attention to this, and so a remonstrance official had to raise it?

sentences.zh: 」即日授刺史者數人。

translations.literal: " That same day several men were appointed prefects.
translations.idiomatic: " That very day several men were appointed prefects.

sentences.zh: 久約又言，宜令親王以下職官遞相推舉，世宗曰：「薦舉人材，惟宰相當為耳，他官品雖高，豈能皆有知人之監？

translations.literal: Jiuyue also said that princes of the blood and officials below them should recommend one another in turn. Shizong said, "Recommending talent is solely what the chancellor ought to do; though other officials' ranks may be high, how can they all possess the discernment to know men?
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyue further proposed that imperial princes and officials beneath them should recommend one another in rotation. Shizong replied, "Recommending talent is the chancellor's duty alone. However high another official's rank may be, can they all truly know how to judge men?

sentences.zh: 方今縣令最闕，宜令刺史以上舉可為縣令者，朕將察其實能而用之。

translations.literal: At present county magistrates are most lacking; it is fitting to have prefects and above recommend those who could serve as county magistrates—I shall examine their real ability and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrates are the greatest shortage just now. Let prefects and higher officials recommend men fit to serve as magistrates; I shall examine their real ability before appointing them.

sentences.zh: 」又謂久約曰：「近日察舉好官，皆是諸科監臨，全無進士，何也？

translations.literal: " He also said to Jiuyue, "Recently, in inspection and recommendation of good officials, all have been from the various specialized examination tracks serving as supervisors—there are no jinshi at all. Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked Jiuyue, "In recent inspections the good officials recommended have all come from the specialized examination tracks serving as supervisors; not one jinshi. Why is that?

sentences.zh: 豈薦舉之法已有奸弊，不可久行乎？

translations.literal: Has the recommendation system already developed corrupt abuses and cannot be continued long?
translations.idiomatic: Has the recommendation system already become corrupt and unsustainable?

sentences.zh: 」久約曰：「諸科中豈無廉能人，不因察舉有終身不至縣令者，此法未可廢也。

translations.literal: " Jiuyue said, "Among the specialized tracks are there not honest and capable men? Without inspection and recommendation some spend their lives never reaching county magistrate—this method must not yet be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiuyue replied, "The specialized tracks surely contain honest and capable men. Without inspection and recommendation, some spend their whole lives never reaching a county magistracy. The system must not be abolished yet.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「爾舉孫必福是乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Did you recommend Sun Bifu?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "Was it you who recommended Sun Bifu?

sentences.zh: 」久約曰：「臣頃任磁州時，必福為武安丞，臣見其廉潔向公，無所顧避，所以保舉。

translations.literal: " Jiuyue said, "When I recently served in Cizhou, Bifu was assistant magistrate of Wu'an; I saw him honest and devoted to the public good, with nothing he would shrink from, and therefore recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiuyue said, "When I was prefect of Cizhou, Bifu was assistant magistrate in Wu'an. I saw him scrupulously honest and devoted to public duty, fearless in doing what was right, and recommended him on that basis.

sentences.zh: 不謂必福既任警巡使，處決凝滯。

translations.literal: I did not expect that once Bifu took the post of patrol commissioner, his judgments would become sluggish and obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: I never imagined that once appointed patrol commissioner he would become so slow and obstructive in his judgments.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「必福非獨遲緩，亦全不解事，所以罪不及保官者，幸其無贓汙耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Bifu is not only slow—he also utterly fails to understand affairs; the reason punishment does not reach the recommending official is simply that fortunately he has no corruption.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Bifu is not merely dilatory; he understands nothing at all. The reason the recommending official is not punished is simply that, fortunately, there was no bribery involved.

sentences.zh: 」久約無以對。

translations.literal: " Jiuyue had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiuyue had no reply.

sentences.zh: 必福五經出身，蓋諸科人，故上問及之。

translations.literal: Bifu had entered office through the Five Classics track—he was a man of the specialized examinations—hence the emperor's question touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: Bifu had entered service through the Five Classics examination track, a specialized-track graduate, which is why the emperor raised the matter.

sentences.zh: 翌日侍朝，故事，宰相奏事則近臣退避，久約欲趨出，世宗止之，自是諫臣不避，以為常。

translations.literal: The next day he attended court. By precedent, when the chancellor reported affairs the close attendants withdrew; Jiuyue was about to hurry out, but Shizong stopped him. From then on remonstrance officials did not withdraw—this became the custom.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, while attending court, Jiuyue moved to withdraw as custom required when the chancellor was reporting affairs. Shizong stopped him. From then on remonstrance officials no longer withdrew during such reports, and this became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，久約以國富民貧、本輕末重、任人太雜、吏權太重、官鹽價高、坊場害民、與夫選左右、擇守令八事為獻，皆嘉納之。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Jiuyue presented eight matters: the state rich but the people poor, root light and branches heavy, employment of men too mixed, clerical power too heavy, official salt prices high, monopoly workshops harming the people, and moreover selecting those close at hand and choosing prefects and magistrates—all were praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, Jiuyue submitted eight policy proposals: the state was rich while the people were poor; the economic base was undervalued and commerce overweighted; appointments were too indiscriminate; clerical authority was too great; official salt prices were too high; state monopolies harmed the people; and, finally, the court should choose its close advisers carefully and appoint prefects and magistrates wisely. Zhangzong praised and adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 再乞致仕，不許，授橫海軍節度使以優佚之。

translations.literal: He again begged to retire from office; this was not permitted, and he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Transverse Sea Army to honor him with ease.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested retirement, but was refused and instead appointed Military Commissioner of the Transverse Sea Army—a post meant to honor him with ease.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he retired from office and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired in the second year of Mingchang and died.

sentences.zh: 久約雋朗敢言，性友弟，為文典贍，有外祖之風雲。

translations.literal: Jiuyue was refined, bright, and daring in speech; by nature he was fraternal among brothers; in writing he was classical and ample, possessing the literary manner of his maternal grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyue was refined, sharp-witted, and fearless in remonstrance; he was devoted to his brothers by nature; his writing was classical and polished, in the literary manner of his maternal grandfather.

sentences.zh: 李晏，字致美，澤州高平人。

translations.literal: Li Yan, styled Zhiwei, was a man of Gaoping in Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, whose courtesy name was Zhiwei, came from Gaoping in Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 性警敏，倜儻尚氣。

translations.literal: By nature he was alert and keen, unconventional and valuing spirited conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted by nature, unconventional, and drawn to bold, spirited action.

sentences.zh: 皇統六年，登經義進士第。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Huangtong he attained jinshi rank in the Classics Meaning examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Huangtong he passed the jinshi examination in Classics Meaning.

sentences.zh: 調岳陽丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant magistrate of Yueyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as assistant magistrate in Yueyang.

sentences.zh: 再轉遼陽府推官，曆中牟令。

translations.literal: After a second transfer he became investigating officer of Liaoyang Prefecture and served as magistrate of Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: After a second transfer he became investigating officer in Liaoyang Prefecture and later served as magistrate of Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 會海陵方營汴京，運木于河，晏領之。

translations.literal: It happened that Hailing was then building Bianjing and transporting timber on the river; Yan took charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: While Hailing was building his capital at Bianjing and shipping timber along the river, Yan was put in charge of the operation.

sentences.zh: 晏以經三門之險，前後失敗者眾，乃馳白行台，以其木散投之水，使工取於下流，人皆便之。

translations.literal: Yan, because passing the three gates was perilous and many had failed before and after, hurried to report to the Branch Secretariat, had the timber cast scattered into the water, and had workers take it from downstream—all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Because the three river gates were treacherous and many shipments had failed there, Yan urgently reported to the Branch Secretariat, had the logs released into the current, and had workers recover them downstream. Everyone found the method far more workable.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，召補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was summoned to fill a clerk post in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother and completing the mourning period, he was summoned to serve as a clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 辭去，為衛州防禦判官。

translations.literal: He resigned and became defense judge of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned the post and became defense judge in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗素識其才名，尋召為應奉翰林文字，特令詣閣謝，上顧謂左右曰：「李晏精神如舊。

translations.literal: Shizong had long known his talent and reputation; soon he was summoned as Attendant-for-Service Hanlin Scribe, and was specially ordered to come to the palace to give thanks. The emperor turned and said to those beside him, "Li Yan's spirit is as of old.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had long known his reputation for talent. Soon Yan was summoned as Attendant-for-Service Hanlin Scribe and was specially ordered to come to the palace to give thanks. The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Li Yan's vigor is unchanged.

sentences.zh: 」慰勞甚悉。

translations.literal: " He comforted and encouraged him very fully.
translations.idiomatic: " He comforted and encouraged him at length.

sentences.zh: 時方議郊禮，命攝太常博士，俄而真授。

translations.literal: At the time the suburban sacrifice was under discussion; he was ordered to act as Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and soon received the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: While the suburban sacrifice was being planned, he was appointed acting Doctor in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and soon received the substantive post.

sentences.zh: 為高麗讀冊官，五遷秘書少監，兼尚書禮部郎中，除西京副留守。

translations.literal: He served as reader of the investiture document for Goryeo, was promoted five times to Vice Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Director in the Ministry of Rites of the Ministry of Works, and was appointed Deputy Protector-General of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served as reader of the investiture document for Goryeo, rose through five promotions to Vice Director of the Palace Library, held a concurrent post as Director in the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed Deputy Protector-General of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂侍臣曰：「翰林舊人少，新進士類不學，至於詔赦冊命之文鮮有能者，可選外任有文章士為之。

translations.literal: Shizong said to his attending ministers, "In the Hanlin the old hands are few; the newly advanced jinshi for the most part do not study—as for edicts of amnesty and investiture documents, there are scarcely any who can write them. We may select men of literary ability serving outside the capital for this.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong told his attendants, "The Hanlin has too few veterans, and recent jinshi generally do not study. Hardly any of them can draft edicts of amnesty or investiture documents. We should select men of proven literary ability from outside appointments.

sentences.zh: 」左右舉晏，上曰：「李晏朕所自識。

translations.literal: " Those beside him recommended Yan; the emperor said, "Li Yan is one I have personally known.
translations.idiomatic: " His attendants recommended Yan. The emperor said, "Li Yan is a man I know personally.

sentences.zh: 」於是召為翰林直學士，兼太常少卿。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was summoned as Hanlin Academician Expositor, concurrently Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan was then summoned as Hanlin Academician Expositor, with a concurrent post as Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞歸養，授鄭州防禦使，未赴，母卒。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he begged to return home to support her; he was appointed Defense Commissioner of Zhengzhou, but before he took up the post his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly he asked to return home to care for her and was appointed Defense Commissioner of Zhengzhou, but before he could take up the post his mother died.

sentences.zh: 起複為翰林直學士。

translations.literal: He was recalled from mourning to serve again as Hanlin Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from mourning and reappointed Hanlin Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 世宗禦後閣，召晏讀新進士所對策，至「縣令闕員取之何道」，上曰：「朕夙夜思此，未知所出。

translations.literal: Shizong held court in the rear pavilion and summoned Yan to read the policy responses of the newly advanced jinshi; when it came to "By what means should vacant county magistrate posts be filled?" the emperor said, "I have thought on this day and night, but do not know the way out.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong held court in the rear pavilion and had Yan read aloud the policy essays of the newly passed jinshi. When they reached the question of how to fill vacant county magistrate posts, the emperor said, "I have pondered this day and night, yet I still do not see the answer.

sentences.zh: 」晏對曰：「臣伏念久矣，但無路不敢言。

translations.literal: " Yan replied, "Your subject has pondered this prostrate for a long time, but had no avenue and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan replied, "Your subject has long brooded over this in private, but had no avenue to speak and dared not do so.

sentences.zh: 今幸待罪侍從，得承大問，願竭所知。

translations.literal: Now, fortunately bearing guilt while attending in attendance, I have received the great question and wish to exhaust what I know.
translations.idiomatic: Now, by good fortune, I stand in attendance before you and may answer your great question; I wish to offer all I know.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然則何如？

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Then what would you propose?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked, "Then what do you propose?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「國朝設科取士，始分南北兩選，北選百人，南選百五十人，合二百五十人。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Our dynasty established examinations to select scholars; at first it divided into two selections, north and south—the north selection took one hundred men, the south selection one hundred fifty, totaling two hundred fifty.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "When our dynasty first established examinations, it held separate northern and southern selections: one hundred candidates in the north, one hundred fifty in the south, two hundred fifty in all.

sentences.zh: 詞賦經義入仕之人既多，所以縣令未嘗闕員。

translations.literal: Those entering office through rhapsody-composition and classics-meaning examinations were numerous, and therefore county magistrate posts were never vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Because many men entered office through both the rhapsody and classics examinations, county magistrate posts were never left vacant.

sentences.zh: 其後南北通選，止設詞賦一科，每舉限取六七十人。

translations.literal: Afterward north and south were combined in one selection, with only the rhapsody examination established; each round was limited to taking sixty or seventy men.
translations.idiomatic: Later the north and south selections were merged, leaving only the rhapsody examination, with a quota of only sixty or seventy graduates each round.

sentences.zh: 入仕之人既少，縣令闕員，蓋由此也。

translations.literal: Those entering office were few, and county magistrate vacancies—this is probably the reason.
translations.idiomatic: With far fewer men entering office, county magistrate vacancies followed—and that is the root of the problem.

sentences.zh: 」上以為然，詔後取人毋限以數。

translations.literal: " The emperor considered this correct and decreed that hereafter recruitment should not be limited by number.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and ordered that future examinations no longer be limited by a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 尋擢吏部侍郎，兼前職，諭旨曰：「卿性果敢，有激揚之意，故以授卿，宜加審慎，毋涉荒唐。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, retaining his former post; an instruction said, "Your nature is bold and decisive, with a mind to rouse and advance—therefore this is conferred on you; you should add careful deliberation and not involve yourself in the absurd.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel while keeping his former post. An instruction read: "You are bold and decisive by nature and inclined to drive matters forward; that is why this post is given you. Be more careful, and do not let your conduct become reckless.

sentences.zh: 」俄為中都路推排使，遷翰林侍講學士，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: " Soon he became Land-Survey Commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit, was transferred to Hanlin Academician Lecturer, and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was made Land-Survey Commissioner for the Central Capital Circuit, then promoted to Hanlin Academician Lecturer with a concurrent appointment as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會朝士以病謁告，世宗意其詐，謂晏曰：「卿素剛正，今某詐病，以宰相親故，畏而不糾歟？

translations.literal: It happened that a court gentleman requested leave on grounds of illness; Shizong suspected fraud and said to Yan, "You have always been upright and firm—now so-and-so feigns illness; because he is a relative of the chancellor, do you fear him and fail to impeach?
translations.idiomatic: When a court official took sick leave, Shizong suspected fraud and said to Yan, "You have always been upright. This man is feigning illness. Because he is related to the chancellor, are you afraid to impeach him?

sentences.zh: 」晏跪對曰：「臣雖老，平生所恃者，誠與直爾。

translations.literal: " Yan knelt and replied, "Though your subject is old, what he has relied on all his life is sincerity and uprightness alone.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan knelt and answered, "Though I am old, all my life I have relied on sincerity and uprightness alone.

sentences.zh: 百官病告，監察當視。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials take sick leave, the surveillance censors ought to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: When officials take sick leave, the surveillance censors are supposed to verify it.

sentences.zh: 臣為中丞，官吏奸私則當言之。

translations.literal: Your subject, as Censor-in-Chief, when officials are corrupt or self-seeking ought to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: As Censor-in-Chief, it is my duty to report official corruption and self-dealing.

sentences.zh: 病而在告，此小事臣容有不知，其畏宰相何圖焉。

translations.literal: Illness and leave on report—on such small matters your subject may perhaps not have known; what would he gain by fearing the chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: Sick leave is a minor matter; I may simply not have known of it. What would I gain by fearing the chancellor?

sentences.zh: 」既出，世宗目送之，曰：「晏年老，氣猶未衰。

translations.literal: " After he withdrew, Shizong watched him go and said, "Yan is old, yet his spirit has not yet declined.
translations.idiomatic: " After Yan withdrew, Shizong watched him leave and remarked, "Yan is old, yet his spirit has not faded.

sentences.zh: 」一日，御史台奏請增監察員，上曰：「采察內外官吏，固系監察。

translations.literal: " One day the Censorate memorialized requesting additional surveillance censors; the emperor said, "Investigating officials within and without is indeed the charge of surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: " One day the Censorate requested additional surveillance censors. The emperor said, "Investigating officials inside and outside the court is indeed the duty of surveillance censors.

sentences.zh: 然爾等有所聞知，亦當彈劾。

translations.literal: Yet when you have heard or learned of something, you also ought to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: But whenever you learn of wrongdoing, you should impeach as well.

sentences.zh: 況糾正非違，台官職也，苟不能正其身，如正人何？

translations.literal: Moreover, correcting wrongdoing is the duty of censorial officials—if you cannot rectify yourselves, how can you rectify others?
translations.idiomatic: Correcting misconduct is the censor's office. If you cannot set your own conduct straight, how can you set others straight?

sentences.zh: 」顧謂晏曰：「豳王年少未練，朕以台事委卿，當一一用意。」

translations.literal: " He turned and said to Yan, "Prince of Bin is young and not yet practiced; I entrust censorial affairs to you—you must attend to each matter with care."
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to Yan and said, "The Prince of Bin is young and inexperienced. I entrust the Censorate to you; attend to every matter with care."

sentences.zh: 初，錦州龍宮寺，遼主撥賜戶民俾輸稅於寺，歲久皆以為奴，有欲訴者害之島中。

translations.literal: Earlier, at Longgong Temple in Jinzhou, the Liao ruler had allotted households to pay taxes to the temple; over the years all were treated as slaves, and those who wished to appeal were killed on an island.
translations.idiomatic: At Longgong Temple in Jinzhou, the Liao emperor had assigned households to pay taxes to the monastery. Over time they were all treated as slaves, and anyone who tried to appeal was killed on a remote island.

sentences.zh: 晏乃具奏：「在律，僧不殺生，況人命乎！

translations.literal: Yan then submitted a full memorial: "By law monks do not take life—how much less human life!
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted a detailed memorial: "By law monks must not take life—how much less a human life!

sentences.zh: 遼以良民為二稅戶，此不道之甚也，今幸遇聖朝，乞盡釋為良。

translations.literal: The Liao made good commoners into dual-tax households—this is the height of inhuman conduct; now, fortunately encountering the sage dynasty, I beg that all be released as good commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao turned free commoners into dual-tax dependents—an outrage. Now that we have a sage dynasty, I beg that they all be restored to free commoner status.

sentences.zh: 」世宗納其言，於是獲免者六百餘人。

translations.literal: " Shizong accepted his words, and thus more than six hundred persons obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong accepted his proposal, and more than six hundred people were freed.

sentences.zh: 故同判大睦親府事謀衍家有民質券，積其息不能償，因沒為奴，屢訴有司不能直，至是，投匭自言。

translations.literal: Formerly the household of Mouyan, Associate Administrator of the Great Office of Imperial Kin, held a commoner's pawn ticket; interest accumulated until it could not be repaid, and he was therefore enslaved; he repeatedly appealed to the authorities without obtaining justice—at this time he cast a petition into the suggestion box and spoke for himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the household of Mouyan, former Associate Administrator of the Great Office of Imperial Kin, a commoner had pledged himself on a pawn ticket. Interest piled up until he could not repay it and was seized as a slave. He appealed repeatedly without obtaining justice; at last he submitted a petition through the public suggestion box.

sentences.zh: 事下御史台，晏檢擿案狀得其情，遂奏免之。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Censorate; Yan examined and extracted the case records, obtained the facts, and memorialized to release him.
translations.idiomatic: The case was referred to the Censorate. Yan examined the records, established the facts, and memorialized for the man's release.

sentences.zh: 尋為賀宋正旦國信副使。

translations.literal: Soon he served as deputy trust envoy to congratulate the Song on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as deputy trust envoy to offer New Year's congratulations to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 及世宗不豫，命宿禁中，一時詔冊，皆晏為之。

translations.literal: When Shizong fell ill, he was ordered to lodge in the inner palace; for a time all edicts and investiture documents were composed by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong fell gravely ill, Yan was ordered to remain in the inner palace, and for a time he drafted all edicts and investiture documents.

sentences.zh: 章宗立，晏畫十事以上。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Yan drafted ten matters and presented them above.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, Yan submitted a memorial outlining ten policy proposals.

sentences.zh: 一曰風俗奢忄栗，宜定制度。

translations.literal: First, customs are extravagant and dissolute—institutions ought to be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: First, popular customs have grown extravagant; institutions should be established to restrain them.

sentences.zh: 二曰禁遊手。

translations.literal: Second, prohibit idlers.
translations.idiomatic: Second, idlers and loafers should be prohibited.

sentences.zh: 三曰宜停鑄錢。

translations.literal: Third, coin casting ought to be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the minting of coin should be stopped.

sentences.zh: 四曰免上戶管庫。

translations.literal: Fourth, exempt upper households from managing storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, upper households should be exempted from managing state storehouses.

sentences.zh: 五曰太平宜興禮樂。

translations.literal: Fifth, in an age of great peace rites and music ought to be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, in this age of peace, rites and music should be revived.

sentences.zh: 六曰量輕租稅。

translations.literal: Sixth, consider lightening land tax and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, land tax and levies should be reduced where possible.

sentences.zh: 七曰減鹽價。

translations.literal: Seventh, reduce the price of salt.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the price of salt should be lowered.

sentences.zh: 八曰免監官陪納虧欠。

translations.literal: Eighth, exempt supervising officials from making up shortages out of their own funds.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, supervising officials should not be required to cover revenue shortfalls from their own pockets.

sentences.zh: 九曰有司尚苟且，乞申明經久遠圖。

translations.literal: Ninth, the responsible offices still favor expediency—I beg that long-term plans be clarified and proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, government offices still favor short-term expediency; I beg that long-term policy be clearly proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 十曰禁網差密，宜尚寬大。

translations.literal: Tenth, prohibitions and nets are rather tight—it is fitting to esteem leniency and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, prohibitions are too tight; the government should favor leniency and breadth.

sentences.zh: 又奏「乞委待制党懷英、修撰張行簡更直進讀陳言文字，以廣視聽」。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "I beg that Academician-in-Waiting Dang Huaiying and Compiler Zhang Xingjian be assigned in rotation to read submitted memorials aloud, so as to broaden what is seen and heard."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that Academician-in-Waiting Dang Huaiying and Compiler Zhang Xingjian take turns reading submitted memorials aloud to broaden the court's awareness.

sentences.zh: 皆採納之。

translations.literal: All were adopted and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 以年老乞致仕，改禮部尚書，兼翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: Because of old age he begged to retire from office; he was changed to Minister of Rites and concurrently Chief Academician of the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his age, he requested retirement and was appointed Minister of Rites with a concurrent post as Chief Academician of the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 越二年，複申前請，授沁南軍節度使，久之，致仕。

translations.literal: After two years he again submitted his former request and was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qinnan Army; after a long time he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he renewed his retirement request and was appointed Military Commissioner of the Qinnan Army; after some time he finally retired.

sentences.zh: 上念其先朝舊人，複起為昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that he was an old man of the former court, recalled him to serve as Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that he was a veteran of the previous reign, the emperor recalled him as Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 明昌六年，歸老，得疾，詔除其子左司員外郎仲略為澤州刺史，以便侍養。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Mingchang he returned home in old age and fell ill; an edict appointed his son, Left Department Vice Director Zhonglüe, as Prefect of Zezhou so that he might attend and support him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Mingchang he retired home and fell ill. An edict appointed his son Zhonglüe, Vice Director in the Left Department, prefect of Zezhou so he could care for his father nearby.

sentences.zh: 承安二年卒，年七十五，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Cheng'an, aged seventy-five; his posthumous title was Wénjiǎn.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Cheng'an at the age of seventy-five. His posthumous title was Wénjiǎn (Cultured and Simple).

sentences.zh: 子 仲略

translations.literal: Son: Zhonglüe
translations.idiomatic: His son: Zhonglüe

sentences.zh: 仲略，字簡之。

translations.literal: Zhonglüe, styled Jianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglüe, whose courtesy name was Jianzhi.

sentences.zh: 聰敏力學，登大定十九年詞賦進士第，調代州五台主簿。

translations.literal: Clever and keen, he studied with effort; in the nineteenth year of Dading he attained jinshi rank in the rhapsody examination and was appointed chief clerk of Wutai in Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and diligent in study, he passed the jinshi rhapsody examination in the nineteenth year of Dading and was posted as chief clerk in Wutai, Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去，服闋，轉韓州軍事判官，遷澤州晉城令，補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he transferred to military judge of Hanzhou, was promoted to magistrate of Jincheng in Zezhou, and was appointed clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother. When mourning ended he became military judge in Hanzhou, was promoted to magistrate of Jincheng in Zezhou, and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 除翰林修撰，兼太常博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Compiler, concurrently Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Compiler with a concurrent post as Doctor in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 改授左司都事，為立夏國王讀冊官。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Chief Clerk of the Left Department and served as reader of the investiture document for the king of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Chief Clerk of the Left Department and served as reader of the investiture document for the king of Xia.

sentences.zh: 還，權領左司。

translations.literal: On his return he acted as head of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served as acting head of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 一日，奏事退，上顧謂侍臣曰：「仲略精神明健，如俊鶻脫帽。

translations.literal: One day, after he had reported affairs and withdrawn, the emperor turned and said to his attendants, "Zhonglüe's spirit is bright and vigorous, like a fine hawk casting off its hood.
translations.idiomatic: One day, after Zhonglüe had reported on business and withdrawn, the emperor remarked to his attendants, "Zhonglüe's spirit is bright and vigorous, like a fine hawk shaking off its hood.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「李仲略健吏也。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Li Zhonglüe is a capable official.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "Li Zhonglüe is a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，轉員外郎，以親病求侍，特授澤州刺史以便祿養。

translations.literal: " Before long he was transferred to Vice Director; because a parent was ill he begged to attend them and was specially appointed Prefect of Zezhou for convenient salary and support.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was promoted to Vice Director. When a parent fell ill he asked to stay nearby and was specially appointed prefect of Zezhou so he could support them on a comfortable stipend.

sentences.zh: 先是，晏領沁南軍節度使，澤于懷為支郡，父子相繼，鄉人榮之。

translations.literal: Earlier Yan had held the post of Military Commissioner of the Qinnan Army; Ze Prefecture in Huai was a subordinate commandery, and father and son succeeded one another—the people of their home district took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yan had served as Military Commissioner of the Qinnan Army, and Ze Prefecture in Huai was under that jurisdiction. Father and son holding office in succession was a source of pride in their home district.

sentences.zh: 以父喪免，起為戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on mourning for his father; he was recalled to serve as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father, then was recalled from mourning as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時上命六品以上官，十日以次轉對，乃進言曰：「凡救其末，不若正其本。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor ordered officials of the sixth rank and above to take turns in audience every ten days; he then advanced and said, "In all cases, to remedy the branches is not as good as setting right the root.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ordered officials of the sixth rank and above to take turns presenting policy views every ten days. Zhonglüe spoke up: "To treat symptoms is never as effective as addressing the root cause.

sentences.zh: 所謂本者厚風俗，去冗食，養財用而已。

translations.literal: What is called the root is nothing more than enriching customs, removing redundant consumption, and nurturing wealth and resources.
translations.idiomatic: The root lies in strengthening public morals, eliminating wasteful consumption, and building up the state's resources.

sentences.zh: 厚風俗在乎立制度，禁奢忄栗。

translations.literal: Enriching customs lies in establishing institutions and prohibiting extravagance and dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: To strengthen morals we must establish institutions and curb extravagance.

sentences.zh: 去冗食在乎寵力農，抑遊墮。

translations.literal: Removing redundant consumption lies in favoring and supporting agriculture and restraining idlers and the fallen.
translations.idiomatic: To cut waste we must favor agriculture and restrain idlers and loafers.

sentences.zh: 養財用在乎廣儲蓄，時斂散。

translations.literal: Nurturing wealth and resources lies in broadening storage and timely gathering and dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: To build up resources we must expand storage and regulate collection and distribution in good time.

sentences.zh: 商賈不通難得之貨，工匠不作無用之器，則下知重本。

translations.literal: If merchants do not circulate hard-to-obtain goods and artisans do not make useless implements, then those below will know to esteem the root.
translations.idiomatic: If merchants do not traffic in rare luxuries and artisans do not make useless goods, the people will learn to value the fundamentals of production.

sentences.zh: 下知重本，則末息矣。

translations.literal: When those below know to esteem the root, the branches will cease.
translations.idiomatic: When the people value the fundamentals, secondary pursuits will naturally decline.

sentences.zh: 」又條陳制度之宜，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " He also itemized what was fitting in institutions; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " He also laid out specific institutional reforms. The emperor praised and adopted them.

sentences.zh: 俄授翰林直學士，兼前職，因命充經義讀卷官。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Hanlin Academician Expositor, retaining his former post, and was therefore ordered to serve as reader of classics-meaning examination papers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Hanlin Academician Expositor while keeping his former post, and was assigned to read classics-meaning examination papers.

sentences.zh: 上問曰：「有司以謂經義不若詞賦，罷之何如？

translations.literal: The emperor asked, "The responsible offices say that classics meaning is not equal to rhapsody composition—how would it be to abolish it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "The ministries say the classics examination is inferior to the rhapsody examination. Should we abolish it?

sentences.zh: 」仲略奏曰：「經乃聖人之書，明經所以適用，非詞賦比。

translations.literal: " Zhonglüe memorialized, "The classics are the books of the sages; to clarify the classics is to make them applicable—it is not comparable to rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhonglüe replied, "The classics are the writings of the sages. Mastery of them serves practical governance; they cannot be compared to rhapsody composition.

sentences.zh: 乞自今以經義進士為考試官，庶得碩學之士。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on jinshi in classics meaning serve as examination officials, so that we may obtain men of great learning.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that henceforth classics jinshi serve as examination examiners, so we may obtain truly learned men.

sentences.zh: 」上可其奏。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 改吏部郎中，遷侍郎，兼翼王傅，俄兼宛王傅。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, promoted to Vice Minister, concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Yi, and soon concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Wan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted to Vice Minister, with concurrent posts as tutor to the Prince of Yi and soon the Prince of Wan.

sentences.zh: 時知大興府事紇石烈執中坐贓，上命仲略鞫之，罪當削解。

translations.literal: At the time Heshenilie Zhizhong, administrator of Daxing Prefecture, was convicted of corruption; the emperor ordered Zhonglüe to interrogate him, and the offense warranted dismissal and degradation.
translations.idiomatic: Heshenilie Zhizhong, administrator of Daxing Prefecture, was found guilty of corruption. The emperor ordered Zhonglüe to investigate; the offense warranted dismissal and degradation.

sentences.zh: 權要競言太重，上頗然之，仲略奏曰：「教化之行，自近者始。

translations.literal: Powerful figures all said the penalty was too heavy; the emperor was rather inclined to agree. Zhonglüe memorialized, "The carrying out of moral transformation begins with what is near.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful figures protested that the penalty was too harsh, and the emperor was inclined to agree. Zhonglüe argued, "Moral transformation must begin close at hand.

sentences.zh: 京師，四方之則也。

translations.literal: The capital is the model for the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the model for the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 郡縣守令無慮數百，此而不懲，何以勵後？

translations.literal: Prefectural and county magistrates and prefects number no less than several hundred—if this one is not punished, how can later ones be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: There are hundreds of prefects and magistrates across the realm. If this man goes unpunished, how can others be held to account?

sentences.zh: 況執中兇殘很愎，慢上虐下，豈可宥之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Zhizhong is fierce, cruel, obstinate, and perverse, disrespectful to superiors and cruel to subordinates—how can he be pardoned?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Zhizhong is brutal, obstinate, disrespectful to superiors, and cruel to subordinates. He must not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Your words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，授山東東西路按察使。

translations.literal: " Before long he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Shandong East and West Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner for the Shandong East and West Circuits.

sentences.zh: 尋以病訪醫京師，泰和五年卒。

translations.literal: Soon, because of illness, he sought medical treatment in the capital and died in the fifth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went to the capital seeking medical treatment for illness and died in the fifth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，歎曰：「此人于國家宣力多矣，何遽止是耶！

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he sighed and said, "This man has expended much effort for the state—how could he so suddenly stop at this!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard the news, he sighed and said, "This man has served the state with great dedication—how could he die so suddenly!

sentences.zh: 」贈朝列大夫，諡曰襄獻。

translations.literal: " He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Court and his posthumous title was Xiángxiàn.
translations.idiomatic: " He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Court. His posthumous title was Xiángxiàn (Assisting and Offering).

sentences.zh: 仲略性豪邁有父風，剛介特立，不阿權貴，臨事明敏無留滯，故所任以幹濟稱雲。

translations.literal: Zhonglüe's nature was bold and open, with his father's manner; he was upright and independent, not fawning on the powerful and noble; in affairs he was bright and keen without delay or obstruction—therefore in every post he was praised for practical achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglüe was bold and open like his father, upright and independent, never fawning on the powerful. In office he was sharp and decisive, and everywhere he served he was known for getting things done.

sentences.zh: 李愈，字景韓，絳之正平人。

translations.literal: Li Yu, styled Jinghan, was a man of Zhengping in Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, whose courtesy name was Jinghan, came from Zhengping in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 業儒術，中正隆五年詞賦進士第，調河南澠池主簿。

translations.literal: He studied Confucian learning; in the fifth year of Zhenglong of the Zhongdu era he attained jinshi rank in the rhapsody examination and was appointed chief clerk of Mianchi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Trained in Confucian learning, he passed the jinshi rhapsody examination in the fifth year of Zhenglong and was posted as chief clerk in Mianchi, Henan.

sentences.zh: 察廉優等為平陽酒副使，遷冀氏令，累遷解州刺史。

translations.literal: Through integrity inspection in the superior grade he became deputy wine commissioner of Pingyang, was transferred to magistrate of Jishi, and through successive promotions became Prefect of Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rated superior in an integrity inspection, he became deputy wine commissioner in Pingyang, was transferred to magistrate of Jishi, and rose through successive promotions to prefect of Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，召授同知中都路都轉運使事，改同知濟南府。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, he was summoned and appointed Associate Administrator of the Central Capital Circuit Transport Commission, then changed to Associate Administrator of Jinan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, Yu was summoned as Associate Administrator of the Central Capital transport commission, then transferred as Associate Administrator of Jinan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，授曹王傅，兼同知定武軍節度使事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he was appointed Tutor to the Prince of Cao, concurrently Associate Military Commissioner of the Dingwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingchang he was appointed tutor to the Prince of Cao with a concurrent post as Associate Military Commissioner of the Dingwu Army.

sentences.zh: 王奉命宴賜北部，愈從行，還過京師，表言：「諸部所貢之馬，止可委招討司受於界上，量給回賜，務省費以廣邊儲。

translations.literal: The prince received orders to banquet and bestow gifts on the northern tribes; Yu accompanied him. On the return, passing through the capital, he submitted a memorial saying, "The horses presented by the various tribes should only be entrusted to the Pacification Commission to receive at the border, with measured return gifts given—strive to economize expenses so as to broaden frontier stores.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was ordered to host banquets and distribute gifts to the northern tribes, and Yu accompanied him. On the return journey through the capital he memorialized: "Horses presented by the tribes should be received only at the border by the Pacification Commission, with measured return gifts. We must economize to build up frontier stores.

sentences.zh: 擬自臨潢至西夏沿邊創設重鎮十數，仍選猛安謀克勳臣子孫有材力者使居其職，田給于軍者許募漢人佃種，不必遠挽牛頭粟而兵自富強矣。

translations.literal: It is proposed to establish more than ten major garrisons along the frontier from Linhuang to Western Xia, and still to select descendants of meritorious meng'an-mouke families with ability and strength to hold these posts; where fields are allotted to the army, permit recruiting Han people to tenant-farm—there is no need to haul ox-head grain from afar, and the troops will themselves become rich and strong.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed establishing a dozen major garrisons along the frontier from Linhuang to Western Xia, staffing them with capable descendants of meritorious Jurchen commanders, and allowing Han tenants to farm military allotments locally, so troops need not depend on grain hauled from distant depots and the army could become self-sufficient.

sentences.zh: 」上覽其奏，謂宰臣曰：「愈一書生耳，其用心之忠如是。

translations.literal: " The emperor read his memorial and said to the chief ministers, "Yu is only a scholar—yet his loyal intent is like this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read the memorial and told his chief ministers, "Yu is only a scholar, yet his loyalty and concern are so evident.

sentences.zh: 」以表下尚書省議。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Works for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the Ministry of Works for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 會愈遷同知西京留守，過闕複上言，以為「前表儻可采，乞斷自宸衷」，上納用焉。

translations.literal: It happened that Yu was transferred to Associate Protector-General of the Western Capital; passing the palace he again submitted a statement, holding that "if the former memorial may be adopted, I beg that Your Majesty decide from the imperial heart"; the emperor accepted and employed it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was transferred as Associate Protector-General of the Western Capital, he passed through the capital and submitted another appeal: if the earlier proposal was sound, he begged the emperor to decide personally. The emperor adopted it.

sentences.zh: 自是，命五年一宴賜，人以為便。

translations.literal: From then on it was ordered that banquets and gifts be given once every five years—people regarded it as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter banquets and gifts to the tribes were held only once every five years, which people welcomed as a practical reform.

sentences.zh: 改棣州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Defense Commissioner of Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Defense Commissioner of Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授大興府治中，上諭之曰：「卿資歷應得三品，以是員方闕而卿能幹，故用之，當知朕意。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Administrator of Daxing Prefecture; the emperor instructed him, saying, "Your qualifications ought to merit the third rank; because this post is vacant and you are capable, We therefore employ you—you should know Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Daxing Prefecture. The emperor told him, "Your qualifications merit the third rank. This post happened to be vacant and you are capable, which is why you are appointed. You should understand what We expect.

sentences.zh: 」北京提刑副使範楫、知歸德府事鄧儼各舉愈以自代，由是擢河南路提刑使。

translations.literal: " Fan Ji, Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Northern Capital, and Deng Yan, Administrator of Guide Prefecture, each recommended Yu to replace themselves; thereby he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Ji, Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of the Northern Capital, and Deng Yan, Administrator of Guide Prefecture, each recommended Yu as his successor. Yu was therefore promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上言：「隨路提刑司乞留官一員，餘分部巡按。

translations.literal: He submitted above: "For each circuit surveillance commission I beg to leave one official in place while the rest divide into sections for inspection tours.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that each circuit surveillance commission keep one official in residence while the rest conducted regional inspection tours.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「本司見置許州，乞移治南京為便。

translations.literal: " He also said, "This commission is presently located in Xuzhou—I beg to move its seat to Nanjing for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: " He also proposed moving the commission's headquarters from Xuzhou to Nanjing for greater convenience.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: " Both were followed.
translations.idiomatic: " Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 憲台廉察，九路提刑司以愈為最。

translations.literal: In the Censorate's integrity inspection, among the nine circuit surveillance commissions Yu was rated foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In the Censorate's integrity review of the nine circuit surveillance commissions, Yu ranked first.

sentences.zh: 五年，入見，尚書省以聞，上問宰執有何議論，平章政事守貞曰：「李愈言河決事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he came to audience; the Ministry of Works reported it; the emperor asked the chief executives what discussion there had been. Grand Councillor Shouzhen said, "Li Yu spoke of the Yellow River breach.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Yu came to court. When the Ministry of Works reported his audience, the emperor asked the chief ministers what Yu had discussed. Grand Councillor Shouzhen said, "Li Yu spoke about the Yellow River breach.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「愈向陳備禦北邊策。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Yu previously presented strategies for defending the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Yu once presented a plan for defending the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 言甚荒唐。

translations.literal: His words were very absurd.
translations.idiomatic: It was quite absurd.

sentences.zh: 」守貞曰：「愈於見職甚幹。

translations.literal: " Shouzhen said, "Yu is very capable in his present duties.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouzhen said, "Yu is very capable in his current post.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「蓋以其敢為耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Probably because he dares to act.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Probably because he is bold enough to speak his mind.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「李愈論河決事，謂宜遣大臣視護以慰人心，其言良是。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Li Yu on the river breach said that a great minister ought to be sent to oversee and protect so as to comfort people's hearts—his words are truly right.
translations.idiomatic: " He added, "On the river breach, Li Yu argued that a senior minister should be sent to oversee relief work and reassure the people. That was sound advice.

sentences.zh: 」明年，改河平軍節度使。

translations.literal: " The next year he was changed to Military Commissioner of the Heiping Army.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Heiping Army.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，徙順義軍，奏陳屯田利害，上遣使宣諭，仍降金牌俾領其事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an he was transferred to the Shunyi Army; he memorialized setting forth the advantages and disadvantages of military colonies; the emperor sent an envoy to proclaim and instruct, and also bestowed a gold tablet empowering him to lead the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cheng'an he was transferred to the Shunyi Army. He memorialized on the pros and cons of military colonies; the emperor sent an envoy to proclaim his policy and issued a gold tablet authorizing Yu to oversee the project.

sentences.zh: 四年，召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was summoned to serve as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 先是，刑部尚書闕，上以愈為可用，令議之。

translations.literal: Earlier the post of Minister of Punishments had been vacant; the emperor regarded Yu as usable and ordered deliberation on it.
translations.idiomatic: The post of Minister of Punishments had been vacant, and the emperor considered Yu suitable and ordered discussion of the appointment.

sentences.zh: 或言愈病，上曰：「愈比陳言，有退地千里而爭言其功之語，卿等定惡此人多言耶。

translations.literal: Some said Yu was ill; the emperor said, "In Yu's recent memorial there is the saying, 'Retreat a thousand li yet still contend to speak of one's merit'—you surely do not dislike that this man speaks much?
translations.idiomatic: Some said Yu was ill. The emperor replied, "In a recent memorial Yu quoted the saying about retreating a thousand li yet still contending to claim merit. You surely do not dislike a man who speaks so frankly?

sentences.zh: 」特召用之。

translations.literal: " He was specially summoned and employed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu was specially summoned and appointed.

sentences.zh: 舊制，陳言者漏所言事於人，並行科罪，仍給告人賞。

translations.literal: By old regulation, if a memorial submitter leaked what he had spoken of to others, punishment was applied in both cases, and the informant was still given a reward.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, if a memorial submitter leaked the content of his submission, both parties were punished and the informant received a reward.

sentences.zh: 愈言：「此蓋所以防閑小人也。

translations.literal: Yu said, "This was surely to guard against petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yu argued, "That rule was meant to guard against petty men.

sentences.zh: 比年以來詔求直言，及命朝臣轉對，又許外路官言事，此皆聖言樂聞忠讜之意，請除去舊條以廣言路。

translations.literal: In recent years edicts have sought forthright speech, and court ministers have been ordered to take turns in audience; outer-circuit officials are also permitted to speak on affairs—all this is the sage intent to delight in hearing loyal remonstrance; I beg to remove the old article so as to broaden the avenue of speech.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the court has sought frank counsel, ordered ministers to present views in rotation, and allowed provincial officials to submit memorials—all signs that the throne welcomes loyal remonstrance. I beg that the old rule be abolished to broaden the avenue of speech.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised and adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋為賀宋正旦副使。

translations.literal: Soon he served as deputy envoy to congratulate the Song on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as deputy envoy to offer New Year's congratulations to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年春，上將幸長樂川，愈切諫曰：「方今戍卒貧弱，百姓騷然，三叉尤近北陲，恆防外患。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Taihe the emperor was about to visit Changle River; Yu urgently remonstrated, saying, "At present the garrison soldiers are poor and weak, the common people are unsettled, and Sancha is especially close to the northern frontier—we must always guard against external trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Taihe the emperor planned to visit Changle River. Yu urgently remonstrated: "Garrison troops are poor and weak, the people are unsettled, and Sancha lies close to the northern frontier, where external threats are constant.

sentences.zh: 兼聞泰和宮在兩山間，地形狹隘，雨潦遄集，固不若北宮池台之勝，優遊閒適也。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear that Taihe Palace lies between two mountains, the terrain narrow and cramped, rain and flooding quickly gathering—it is certainly not like the superiority of the Northern Palace's pools and terraces for leisurely ease and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Taihe Palace lies between mountains in cramped terrain where rain and flooding gather quickly. It cannot compare with the Northern Palace's pools and terraces for comfortable leisure.

sentences.zh: 」上不從，夏四月，愈複諫曰：「北部侵我舊疆千有餘裏，不謀雪恥，複欲北幸，一旦有警，臣恐丞相襄、樞密副使闍母等不足恃也。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow. In the fourth month of summer Yu again remonstrated, saying, "The northern tribes have encroached on our old territory by more than a thousand li; without planning to wipe away the shame, you again wish to travel north on tour—if there is suddenly an alarm, your subject fears that Chancellor Xiang, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Chanmu, and others may not be sufficient to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not listen. In the fourth month Yu remonstrated again: "The northern tribes have seized more than a thousand li of our old territory. Instead of planning revenge, Your Majesty wishes to tour the north again. If trouble arises, I fear Chancellor Xiang, Vice Commissioner Chanmu, and others may not suffice.

sentences.zh: 況皇嗣未立，群心無定，豈可遠事逸遊哉。

translations.literal: Moreover the imperial heir is not yet established and the hearts of the multitude are unsettled—how can you attend to distant pleasures and roaming travel?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, no heir has been named and public morale is unsettled. How can Your Majesty indulge in distant pleasure travel?

sentences.zh: 」上異其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor was struck by his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was struck by his words.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授河平軍節度使，改知河中府事，致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Heiping Army, changed to Administrator of Hezhong Prefecture, and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Heiping Army, then Administrator of Hezhong Prefecture, and retired.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Taihe, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Taihe at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 諡曰清獻。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Qīngxiàn.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Qīngxiàn (Pure and Offering).

sentences.zh: 自著《狂愚集》二十卷。

translations.literal: He himself authored twenty juan of the Collected Writings of the Mad Fool.
translations.idiomatic: He authored twenty juan of the Collected Writings of the Mad Fool.

sentences.zh: 王賁，字文孺，其先自臨潢移貫宛平。

translations.literal: Wang Ben, styled Wenru—his ancestors moved from Linhuang and established residence in Wanping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ben, whose courtesy name was Wenru, came from a family that had moved from Linhuang and settled in Wanping.

sentences.zh: 曾祖士方，正直敢言。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shifang was upright and daring in speech.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shifang was upright and fearless in speech.

sentences.zh: 遼道宗信樞密使耶律乙辛之讒殺其太子，世無敢白其冤者，士方擊義鐘以訴，遼主感悟，卒誅乙辛，厚賞士方，授承奉官。

translations.literal: Liao Emperor Daozong believed the slander of Privy Councillor Yelü Yixin and killed his crown prince; in the world none dared declare his wrong—Shifang struck the bell of righteousness to appeal; the Liao ruler was moved to understanding, finally executed Yixin, richly rewarded Shifang, and appointed him Attendant-for-Service.
translations.idiomatic: Liao Emperor Daozong believed the slander of Privy Councillor Yelü Yixin and had his crown prince killed. No one dared speak for the prince's innocence until Shifang struck the bell of righteousness to appeal. The Liao emperor was moved, eventually executed Yixin, richly rewarded Shifang, and appointed him Attendant-for-Service.

sentences.zh: 父中安，擢進士第，坐田玨黨事廢。

translations.literal: His father Zhong'an was advanced to jinshi rank but was dismissed on account of the Tian Jue faction affair.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhong'an passed the jinshi examination but was dismissed in the Tian Jue faction purge.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位黨禁解，終沂州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne the faction ban was lifted; he ended as Defense Commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong ascended the throne the faction ban was lifted, and Zhong'an ended his career as Defense Commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 賁性孝友，勤敏好學，第進士，由複州軍事判官補尚書省令史，擢右三部檢法司正。

translations.literal: Ben was filial and fraternal by nature, diligent, keen, and fond of learning; he attained jinshi rank, from military judge of Fuzhou was appointed clerk in the Ministry of Works, and was promoted to Director of the Right Three Departments Inspection and Law Office.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was filial, fraternal, diligent, and studious. After passing the jinshi examination he rose from military judge in Fuzhou to clerk in the Ministry of Works and was promoted to Director of the Right Three Departments Inspection and Law Office.

sentences.zh: 待御史賈鉉舉賁安靜有守，不尚奔競，政府亦言其廉素，善論議。

translations.literal: Awaiting Censor Jia Xuan recommended Ben as quiet and principled, not given to scrambling for advancement; the government also said he was honest and plain, skilled in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting Censor Jia Xuan recommended Ben as steady and principled, not given to scrambling for advancement. The government also praised his integrity and skill in debate.

sentences.zh: 擢河北東西、大名府路提刑判官，選授尚書省都事，以喪去。

translations.literal: He was promoted to surveillance judge of the Hebei East and West and Daming Prefecture circuits, selected and appointed Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, and left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to surveillance judge for the Hebei East and West and Daming Prefecture circuits, then selected as Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Works, and left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 用薦者多，起複刑部員外郎、侍御史，累遷南京路按察使，卒。

translations.literal: Because many recommended him, he was recalled from mourning as Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments and Attending Censor, was repeatedly promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Nanjing Circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of many recommendations he was recalled from mourning as Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments and Attending Censor, rose through successive promotions to Surveillance Commissioner of the Nanjing Circuit, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 賁敦厚尚義，篤於親朋，不營產業，比歿，家甚窶，上聞憫惜之，贈朝列大夫，仍厚恤共家。

translations.literal: Ben was sincere and thick, esteeming righteousness, devoted to kin and friends, and did not manage property; by the time of his death his household was very poor—the emperor heard and pitied him, posthumously granted Grand Master of the Court, and still generously relieved his family.
translations.idiomatic: Ben was sincere and devoted to righteousness and his friends, and never built up private wealth. At his death his household was destitute. The emperor pitied him, posthumously granted him Grand Master of the Court, and gave his family generous relief.

sentences.zh: 弟質，字敬叔，登大定二十五年進士第，累官吏部主事，以才幹舉遷昭義軍節度副使。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhi, styled Jingshu, attained jinshi rank in the twenty-fifth year of Dading, through successive offices became Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and through recommendation for ability was transferred to Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhi, courtesy name Jingshu, passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Dading, rose through posts to Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and was promoted on merit to Vice Military Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 章宗問質臨事若何，張萬公對曰：「勝其兄賁。

translations.literal: Zhangzong asked how Zhi was in handling affairs; Zhang Wangong replied, "He surpasses his elder brother Ben.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong asked how Zhi handled affairs, Zhang Wangong replied, "He surpasses his elder brother Ben.

sentences.zh: 」章宗曰：「及其兄亦可矣。

translations.literal: Zhangzong said, "Reaching his elder brother would also be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong replied, "Being on a par with his elder brother would be commendable enough."

sentences.zh: 」後以禮部尚書致仕，終。

translations.literal: Later he retired as Minister of Rites and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired from office as Minister of Rites and passed away.

sentences.zh: 許安仁

translations.literal: Xu Anren
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Xu Anren

sentences.zh: 許安仁，字子靜，獻州交河人。

translations.literal: Xu Anren, styled Zijing, was a native of Jiaohe in Xian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Anren, whose courtesy name was Zijing, came from Jiaohe in Xian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，能自刻苦讀書，善屬文。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he could apply himself to arduous study and was skilled at composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents early but disciplined himself in study and became an accomplished writer.

sentences.zh: 登大定七年進士第，調河間縣主簿。

translations.literal: He attained jinshi rank in the seventh year of Dading and was assigned as chief clerk of Hejian County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the imperial examinations in the seventh year of the Dading era and took up the post of chief clerk in Hejian County.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常博士，兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became Doctor of the Directorate of Ceremonies and concurrently Compiler of the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Doctor of Ceremonies, serving concurrently as a compiler at the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 章宗為皇太孫，安仁以講學被選東宮，轉左補闕、應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong was Imperial Grandson, Anren was selected for the Eastern Palace for lecturing on learning; he was transferred to Left Remonstrator and Hanlin Attendant-Writer.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhangzong was still imperial grandson, Anren was chosen to lecture in the Eastern Palace; he then became Left Remonstrator and a Hanlin attendant-writer.

sentences.zh: 上即位，改國子監丞，兼補闕，徙翰林修撰，同知制誥，兼職如故。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he was changed to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, concurrently Remonstrator, transferred to Hanlin Compiler and Associate Director of Proclamations; his concurrent posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's accession, he was made Vice Director of the Imperial College while retaining his remonstrator post, then promoted to Hanlin compiler and associate director of proclamations, with his other duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 侍御史賈鉉以安仁守道端愨，薦於朝。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Jia Xuan, on account of Anren's adherence to the Way and upright integrity, recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Jia Xuan recommended Anren to the court, citing his steadfast integrity and moral rectitude.

sentences.zh: 同知濟南府事路伯達繼上章稱其立己純正，宜加顯任，超授禮部郎中，兼左補闕。

translations.literal: Deputy Administrator of Jinan Prefecture Lu Boda subsequently submitted a memorial stating that Anren established himself in pure correctness and ought to receive distinguished appointment; he was exceptionally appointed Director of the Ministry of Rites, concurrently Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Boda, deputy administrator of Jinan, soon followed with a memorial praising Anren's spotless character and urging a prominent appointment; Anren was then skip-promoted to director in the Ministry of Rites while retaining his post as Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 適朝議以流人實邊，安仁言：「昔漢有募民實邊之議，蓋度地營邑，制為田宅，使至者有所居，作者有所用，於是輕去故鄉而易於遷徙。

translations.literal: Just then the court debated using exiled convicts to populate the frontier; Anren said, "In antiquity Han had a proposal to recruit commoners to settle the borderlands—essentially surveying land to establish settlements and allotting fields and dwellings, so that those who arrived had places to live and those who worked had means to use; thus they lightly left their old homes and found relocation easy.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was debating whether to send exiled criminals to populate the frontier, Anren argued, "The Han once considered recruiting settlers for the border by laying out towns, assigning fields and homes, and giving newcomers both shelter and livelihood—making it easier to leave home and resettle.

sentences.zh: 如使被刑之徒寒餓困苦，無聊之心，靡所顧藉，與古之募民實塞不同，非所宜行。

translations.literal: If one makes those who have suffered punishment endure cold, hunger, and hardship, with hearts of despair and nothing to lean upon, this differs from the ancient recruitment of people to fill the frontier passes and is not a policy that ought to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But if punished exiles are left cold, hungry, and desperate, with no support to fall back on, the policy bears no resemblance to the old frontier-recruitment schemes and should not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 明昌四年春，上將幸景明宮，安仁與同列諫曰：「昔漢、唐雖有甘泉、九成避暑之行，然皆去京師不遠。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Mingchang, when the emperor was about to visit Jingming Palace, Anren remonstrated together with his colleagues, saying, "Formerly Han and Tang, though they had summer-retreat journeys to Ganquan and Jiucheng, were never far from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Mingchang 4, as the emperor prepared to visit Jingming Palace, Anren and his colleagues remonstrated: "Han and Tang emperors did travel to Ganquan and Jiucheng to escape the heat, but those palaces lay close to the capital.

sentences.zh: 非如金蓮千里之外，鄰沙漠，隔關嶺，萬一有警，何以應變，此不可不慮也。

translations.literal: It is not like Jinlian, a thousand li away, bordering the desert and separated by frontier passes—if alarm should arise, how would one respond? This is something that cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlian lies a thousand li distant, beside the desert and beyond the mountain passes—if trouble broke out, how could you respond in time? That risk cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，遂罷幸。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the imperial visit was thereupon canceled.
