translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and the planned visit was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 出為澤州刺史，作《無隱論》上之，凡十篇，曰本朝、曰情欲、曰養心、曰田獵、曰公道、曰養源、曰冗官、曰育材、曰限田、曰理財。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Prefect of Ze Prefecture and submitted to the throne "Discourse on Concealing Nothing," ten essays in all, titled "This Dynasty," "Desire and Emotion," "Nourishing the Heart," "Field Hunting," "Public Justice," "Nourishing the Source," "Redundant Officials," "Cultivating Talent," "Limiting Fields," and "Managing Finances."
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Ze Prefecture, he submitted a ten-part treatise called "Discourse on Concealing Nothing," covering the present dynasty, human desires, self-cultivation, hunting, public justice, moral foundations, redundant officials, nurturing talent, land limits, and fiscal management.

sentences.zh: 在郡二年，徙同知河南府事，升汾陽軍節度使，致仕。

translations.literal: After two years in the prefecture, he was transferred to Deputy Administrator of Henan Prefecture, promoted to Military Commissioner of the Fenyang Army, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After two years as prefect, he became deputy administrator of Henan Prefecture, was promoted to military commissioner of the Fenyang Army, and then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 泰和五年卒，年七十七，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Taihe, aged seventy-seven; his posthumous title was Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe 5 at the age of seventy-seven and was posthumously honored as Wenjian, "Cultured and Unadorned."

sentences.zh: 安仁質實無華，澹然有古君子風，故為時人所稱雲。

translations.literal: Anren was plain and sincere without ornament, calmly possessed of the bearing of an ancient gentleman; therefore he was praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Unpretentious and sincere, with the quiet dignity of a classical gentleman, Anren won wide esteem among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 梁襄，字公贊，絳州人。

translations.literal: Liang Xiang, styled Gongzan, was a native of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xiang, whose courtesy name was Gongzan, came from Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤，養于叔父甯。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he was raised by his uncle Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents early and was brought up by his uncle Ning.

sentences.zh: 性穎悟，日記千餘言。

translations.literal: By nature he was quick-witted and could memorize more than a thousand words each day.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally brilliant, he could commit more than a thousand characters to memory in a single day.

sentences.zh: 登大定三年進士第，調耀州同官主簿。

translations.literal: He attained jinshi rank in the third year of Dading and was assigned as chief clerk of Tongguan in Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations in Dading 3 and was appointed chief clerk in Tongguan, Yao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三遷邠州淳化令，有善政。

translations.literal: Through three promotions he became Magistrate of Chunhua in Bin Prefecture and had good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three times, he served as magistrate of Chunhua in Bin Prefecture, where his administration won praise.

sentences.zh: 察廉，升慶陽府推官，召為薛王府掾。

translations.literal: Through integrity inspection he was promoted to Investigating Officer of Qingyang Prefecture and summoned to be an aide in the Prince of Xue's household.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized in an integrity review, he rose to investigating officer in Qingyang Prefecture and was then called to serve as an aide in the household of the Prince of Xue.

sentences.zh: 世宗將幸金蓮川，有司具辦，襄上疏極諫曰：

translations.literal: When Shizong was about to visit Jinlian River, the relevant offices made full preparations; Xiang submitted a memorial remonstrating to the utmost, saying:
translations.idiomatic: As Shizong prepared to visit Jinlian River and the officials made elaborate arrangements, Xiang submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 金蓮川在重山之北，地積陰冷，五穀不殖，郡縣難建，蓋自古極邊荒棄之壤也。

translations.literal: Jinlian River lies north of the layered mountains; the land accumulates yin and cold, the five grains do not grow, and prefectures and counties are hard to establish—it is essentially soil abandoned as utterly frontier and desolate since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Jinlian River lies beyond the northern mountains in a perpetually cold region where grain will not grow and no county can be sustained—a wasteland abandoned since ancient times as the outermost frontier.

sentences.zh: 氣候殊異，中夏降霜，一日之間，寒暑交至，特與上京、中都不同，尤非聖躬將攝之所。

translations.literal: The climate is exceptionally strange: in midsummer frost falls, and within a single day cold and heat alternate in succession; it is entirely unlike the Upper Capital and the Central Capital, and is especially no place for the sacred person to recuperate.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is extreme: frost can fall in midsummer, and heat and cold may alternate within a single day. It is nothing like the Upper or Central Capital and is wholly unsuited to the emperor's health and rest.

sentences.zh: 凡奉養之具無不遠勞飛挽，越山逾險，其費數倍。

translations.literal: All provisions for imperial maintenance must be laboriously transported from afar by convoy, crossing mountains and passing through peril; the expense is several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Every item needed for the imperial household must be hauled from far away over mountains and dangerous passes, at many times the normal cost.

sentences.zh: 至於頓舍之處，軍騎闐塞，主客不分，馬牛風逸以難收，臧獲逋逃而莫得，奪攘蹂躪，未易禁止。

translations.literal: As for places of halt, armies and cavalry crowd and block the way; host and guest are not distinguished; horses and cattle scatter in the wind and are hard to recover; servants flee and cannot be found; plunder and trampling are not easily stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At every stopping place troops and cavalry choke the roads, hosts and guests mingle in confusion, livestock scatter beyond recall, servants desert and vanish, and looting and trampling become impossible to control.

sentences.zh: 公卿百官衛士，富者車帳僅容，貧者穴居露處，輿台皁隸，不免困踣，饑不得食，寒不得衣，一夫致疾，染及眾人，夭傷無辜，何異刃殺。

translations.literal: Among ministers, officials, and guards, the wealthy have carts and tents barely sufficient to hold them, while the poor dwell in caves and sleep in the open; runners and menials cannot escape exhaustion and collapse—hungry yet unable to eat, cold yet unable to clothe themselves; if one man falls ill, the infection spreads to the multitude, and innocent lives are cut short—how is this different from killing by the blade?
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, officials, and guards alike suffer: the wealthy barely fit into their carts and tents, while the poor sleep in caves or out in the open. Runners and servants collapse from hunger and cold; one man's illness spreads to many, and innocent lives are lost—as though they had been slain with swords.

sentences.zh: 此特細故耳，更有大於此者。

translations.literal: These are merely minor matters; there are greater ones than these.
translations.idiomatic: These are only minor hardships; far graver concerns lie ahead.

sentences.zh: 臣聞高城峻池，深居邃禁，帝王之籓籬也，壯士健馬，堅甲利兵，帝王之爪牙也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that high walls and deep moats, dwelling deeply within secluded palaces—these are the fence and barrier of emperors and kings; stalwart warriors and strong horses, firm armor and sharp weapons—these are the claws and fangs of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: I have always understood that high walls, deep moats, and secure palaces are a ruler's first line of defense, while strong soldiers, hardy horses, and sharp weapons are his claws and fangs.

sentences.zh: 今行宮之所，非有高殿廣宇城池之固，是廢其籓籬也。

translations.literal: Now the place of the traveling palace has no high halls, broad halls, or the solidity of walls and moats—this is to discard the fence and barrier.
translations.idiomatic: The temporary palace offers none of the towering halls, broad halls, or fortified walls of the capital—it abandons the ruler's protective barrier.

sentences.zh: 持甲常坐之馬，日暴雨蝕，臣知其必羸瘠矣。

translations.literal: The horses that regularly bear armor and stand ready, daily drenched by violent rain, your subject knows must grow weak and emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: The horses kept saddled and ready are soaked daily by torrential rain; they cannot fail to grow weak and gaunt.

sentences.zh: 禦侮待用之軍，穴居野處，冷啖寒眼，臣知其必疲瘵矣。

translations.literal: The armies kept ready to repel insult dwell in caves and camp in the wild, eating cold food with sleepless cold nights; your subject knows they must grow weary and sickly.
translations.idiomatic: The troops held in reserve to meet attack live in caves and open camps on cold rations and sleepless nights; they too must grow exhausted and ill.

sentences.zh: 衛宮周廬才容數人，一旦霖潦積旬，衣甲弓刀沾濕柔脆，豈堪為用，是失其爪牙也。

translations.literal: The encircling barracks guarding the palace hold only a few men each; once heavy rain and flooding accumulate for ten days, clothing, armor, bows, and blades grow damp, soft, and brittle—how can they be fit for use? This is to lose the claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: The guard barracks around the palace hold only a handful of men each; after weeks of rain, armor, bows, and blades turn sodden and useless—the ruler's claws and fangs are lost.

sentences.zh: 秋杪將歸，人已疲矣，馬已弱矣，裹糧已空，褚衣已弊，猶且遠幸松林，以從畋獵，行於不測之地，往來之間，動逾旬月，轉輸移徙之勞，更倍於前矣。

translations.literal: At the end of autumn, about to return, men are already weary, horses already weak, wrapped provisions already exhausted, stored clothing already worn out—yet still one travels far to visit Songlin to follow the hunt, moving through unpredictable terrain; in going and coming, each journey often exceeds ten days, and the labor of transport and relocation is again twice what it was before.
translations.idiomatic: By late autumn, when men and horses are already exhausted, provisions spent, and clothing in rags, the court still presses on to Songlin for the hunt through uncertain terrain—each round trip taking more than ten days and doubling the burden of transport and relocation.

sentences.zh: 以陛下神武善騎射，舉世莫及，若夫銜橛之變，猛摯之虞，姑置勿論。

translations.literal: Given Your Majesty's divine martial prowess and skill in mounted archery, unmatched in the world, as for the hazard of a bit-ring accident or the fear of a fierce beast's attack, let those be set aside for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's martial skill and horsemanship are unmatched in the world, so I will set aside the risks of a mount throwing its rider or a savage beast striking home.

sentences.zh: 設於行獵之際，烈風暴至，麈埃漲天，宿霧四塞，跬步不辨，以致翠華有崤陵之避、襄城之迷，百官狼狽於道途，衛士參錯于隊伍，當此宸衷寧無戒悔。

translations.literal: Suppose that in the midst of the hunting journey a violent wind suddenly arrives, dust swells to fill the sky, lingering mist blocks on all sides, and a single step cannot be distinguished—so that the imperial carriage has the flight of Xiao Ling and the bewilderment of Xiangcheng, officials are disheveled on the road, and guards are jumbled out of formation; at such a moment, could the imperial heart be without warning and regret?
translations.idiomatic: But if, mid-hunt, a sudden gale whips up blinding dust and fog so that one cannot see a step ahead—the imperial carriage lost as at Xiao Ling or Xiangcheng, officials scattered in disarray on the roads, guards thrown out of rank—would Your Majesty not bitterly regret it?

sentences.zh: 夫神龍不可以失所，人主不可以輕行，良謂此也。

translations.literal: The divine dragon cannot be without its proper place; the ruler of men cannot lightly travel—this is precisely what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: A divine dragon must not leave its proper domain, nor should a sovereign travel lightly—this is exactly my point.

sentences.zh: 所次之宮，草略尤甚，殿宇周垣，唯用氈布。

translations.literal: The palace where one halts is especially crude and rough; the halls and surrounding walls use only felt and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The temporary palaces are shockingly crude—the halls and surrounding walls are made of nothing but felt and cloth.

sentences.zh: 押宿之官、上番之士，終日驅馳，加之饑渴，已不勝倦。

translations.literal: The officials on overnight duty and the soldiers on rotating watch drive and gallop all day; added to hunger and thirst, they already cannot bear the weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Officers on overnight duty and soldiers on rotating watch ride hard all day, hungry and thirsty, already beyond exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 更使徹曙巡警，露坐不眠，精神有限，何以克堪。

translations.literal: They are further made to patrol until dawn breaks, sitting in the open without sleep; spirit and strength are limited—how can they possibly endure?
translations.idiomatic: They are then kept on patrol until dawn, sitting unsheltered without sleep—how can finite strength endure such demands?

sentences.zh: 雖陛下悅以使人，勞而不怨，豈若不勞之為愈也。

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty may please people by employing them and they labor yet do not complain, would it not be better not to labor them?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty wins loyalty through kindness and men labor without complaint, would it not be far better not to impose such labor at all?

sentences.zh: 故君人者不可恃人無異謀，要在處己於無憂患之域也。

translations.literal: Therefore one who rules men cannot rely on others having no divergent designs; the essential thing is to place oneself in a domain free from worry and peril.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler cannot simply trust that no one harbors treacherous designs; the key is to keep himself in a position free from danger.

sentences.zh: 燕都地處雄要，北倚山險，南壓區夏，若坐堂隍，俯視庭宇，本地所生，人馬勇勁，亡遼雖小，止以得燕故能控制南北，坐致宋幣。

translations.literal: The Yan capital occupies a commanding position, leaning on mountain peril to the north and pressing down on the central lands to the south; it is like sitting in a hall terrace and looking down on the courtyard. The men and horses born of this land are brave and strong; though fallen Liao was small, it was only because it held Yan that it could control north and south and sit receiving Song tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yan occupies a strategic position, shielded by mountains to the north and commanding the heartland to the south—like a lord seated in his hall looking down on his court. Its native soldiers and horses are fierce and strong; even fallen Liao, though a small state, controlled north and south and extracted Song tribute precisely because it held Yan.

sentences.zh: 燕蓋京都之選首也。

translations.literal: Yan is essentially the foremost choice among capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Yan is the finest capital a realm could choose.

sentences.zh: 況今又有宮闕井邑之繁麗，倉府武庫之充實，百官家屬皆處其內，非同曩日之陪京也。

translations.literal: Moreover, today there are also the splendor of palaces and market towns, the fullness of granaries and armories, and the families of all officials dwelling within—it is not like the companion capital of former days.
translations.idiomatic: Today Yan boasts splendid palaces and thriving towns, full granaries and arsenals, and the households of the entire bureaucracy—all far more than the secondary capital it once was.

sentences.zh: 居庸、古北、松亭、榆林等關，東西千里，山峻相連，近在都畿，易於據守，皇天本以限中外，開大金萬世之基而設也。

translations.literal: The passes of Juyong, Gubei, Songting, Yulin, and others stretch a thousand li east and west, lofty mountains linked together, close to the capital region and easy to hold—Heaven originally set them to divide inner and outer realms and to open the foundation of Great Jin for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Juyong, Gubei, Songting, and Yulin passes span a thousand li of linked mountain barriers close to the capital, easy to defend—barriers Heaven itself placed between inner and outer realms to secure Great Jin's foundation for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 奈何無事之日，越居草萊，輕不貲之聖躬，愛沙磧之微涼，忽祖宗之大業，此臣所惜也。

translations.literal: Yet in days without incident, why cross into wild grass and weeds, lightly treat the sacred person as of no value, cherish the slight coolness of sandy wastes, and neglect the great enterprise of the ancestors? This is what your subject regrets.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in peacetime you would leave all this to dwell among wild grasses, risk the emperor's precious person for a trace of coolness in the desert, and neglect the ancestral foundation—this is what I lament.

sentences.zh: 又行幸所過，山徑阻修，林穀晻靄，上有縣崖，下多深壑，垂堂之戒，不可不思。

translations.literal: Moreover, along the route of the imperial visit, mountain paths are obstructed and steep, forest valleys dark and misty; above are overhanging cliffs, below are many deep ravines—the warning of standing beneath a falling hall cannot go unconsidered.
translations.idiomatic: The route of the imperial tour passes through steep mountain paths and mist-shrouded valleys, with cliffs overhead and deep ravines below—the ancient warning against standing beneath a collapsing roof must not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 臣聞漢、唐離宮，去長安才百許裏，然武帝幸甘泉，遂中江充之奸，太宗居九成，幾致結社之變。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the detached palaces of Han and Tang were only about a hundred li from Chang'an, yet when Emperor Wu visited Ganquan he fell victim to Jiang Chong's treachery, and when Emperor Taizong stayed at Jiucheng he nearly brought about the Shentu plot.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that Han and Tang pleasure palaces lay barely a hundred li from Chang'an—yet Emperor Wu's visit to Ganquan played into Jiang Chong's conspiracy, and Taizong's stay at Jiucheng nearly triggered the Shentu rebellion.

sentences.zh: 太康畋於洛汭，後羿拒河而失邦；

translations.literal: Tai Kang hunted at the Luo marshes; Hou Yi blocked the river crossing and the state was lost;
translations.idiomatic: Tai Kang went hunting at the Luo marshes; Hou Yi seized the river crossing and the dynasty was lost;

sentences.zh: 魏帝拜陵近郊，司馬懿竊權而篡國。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor worshipped at the tombs in the near suburbs; Sima Yi usurped power and seized the state.
translations.idiomatic: A Wei emperor paid tomb rites in the nearby suburbs while Sima Yi seized power and usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 隋煬、海陵，雖惡德貫盈，人誰敢議？

translations.literal: Sui Yangdi and Prince Hailing, though their wicked virtue filled the measure—who dared to criticize them?
translations.idiomatic: Sui Yangdi and Prince Hailing were steeped in wickedness—yet who dared speak against them?

sentences.zh: 止以離棄宮闕，遠事巡征，其禍遂速，皆可為殷鑒也。

translations.literal: It was only because they abandoned the palace halls, went far on tours and campaigns, and their calamity therefore came swiftly—all can serve as stern mirrors from the past.
translations.idiomatic: They brought ruin upon themselves by abandoning the palace for distant tours and campaigns—their downfall came swiftly, and each offers a sober lesson from history.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗論之：安民濟眾，唐、虞猶難之。

translations.literal: Your subject has once argued: to settle the people and aid the multitude—even Yao and Shun found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: I have argued before that securing the people's welfare—even Yao and Shun found that arduous.

sentences.zh: 而今日之民，賴陛下之英武，無兵革之憂，賴陛下之聖明，無官吏之虐，賴陛下之寬仁，無刑罰之枉，賴陛下之節儉，無賦斂之繁，可謂能安濟矣。

translations.literal: Yet the people of today rely on Your Majesty's heroic martial prowess and have no worry of war; rely on Your Majesty's sagely clarity and have no tyranny from officials; rely on Your Majesty's broad benevolence and have no wrongful punishments; rely on Your Majesty's frugality and have no heavy taxation—it can be said that settling and aiding them has been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Today's people owe their peace to Your Majesty's martial strength, free from the fear of war; to Your Majesty's wisdom, free from official oppression; to Your Majesty's benevolence, free from unjust punishment; and to Your Majesty's frugality, free from crushing taxes—you have already achieved what even Yao and Shun found difficult.

sentences.zh: 而游畋納涼之樂，出於富貴之餘，靜而思動，非如衣食切身有不可去者，罷之至易耳。

translations.literal: Yet the pleasure of roaming, hunting, and seeking coolness arises from surplus wealth and rank; when still one thinks of moving, it is not like food and clothing close to the body that cannot be cast off—to abandon it is extremely easy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the pleasures of touring, hunting, and escaping the heat are luxuries of surplus, not necessities like food and clothing that cannot be forsaken—they would be the easiest thing in the world to give up.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗將行關南，畏魏征而停，漢文帝欲馳霸陵，袁盎諫而遽止。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong of Tang was about to travel south of the pass but stopped for fear of Wei Zheng; Emperor Wen of Han wished to gallop to Baling, but Yuan Ang remonstrated and he immediately halted.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Taizong planned a journey south of the pass but stopped at Wei Zheng's warning; Han Wendi wished to race to Baling but turned back the moment Yuan Ang remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 是陛下能行唐、虞之難行，而未能罷中主之易罷，臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This means Your Majesty can do what Yao and Shun found hard to do, yet cannot abandon what mediocre rulers find easy to abandon—this is what your subject cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty can accomplish what even Yao and Shun found difficult, yet cannot set aside what mediocre rulers readily forsake—I confess I cannot fathom it.

sentences.zh: 且燕京之涼，非濟南之比，陛下牧濟南日，每遇炎蒸，不離府署，今九重之內，台榭高明，宴安穆清，何暑得到。

translations.literal: Moreover, the coolness of Yanjing is not comparable to Jinan; in the days when Your Majesty governed Jinan, whenever heat and steam arose, you did not leave the prefectural office; now within the ninefold palace, terraces and pavilions are lofty and bright, feasting in peace and pure tranquility—how could summer heat reach there?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Yan's coolness is nothing like Jinan's; when Your Majesty governed Jinan, you never left the prefectural yamen even in the worst heat. Now within the palace, lofty terraces and halls offer serene comfort—how could summer heat penetrate there at all?

sentences.zh: 議者謂陛下北幸久矣，每歲隨駕大小，前歌後舞而歸，今茲再出，寧有遽不可乎。

translations.literal: Those who debate say Your Majesty has long made northern visits; each year the great and small follow the imperial carriage, singing before and dancing behind on the return—if one goes out again this year, could it suddenly be impossible?
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that Your Majesty has toured the north for years, with the whole court singing and dancing on each return—surely one more journey could do no harm?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為患生於不戒者多矣，西漢崇用外戚，而有王莽之禍，梁武好納叛降，而有侯景之變。

translations.literal: Your subject foolishly thinks that calamities born from failing to guard against them are many: Western Han exalted and employed maternal kin, and there was the disaster of Wang Mang; Emperor Wu of Liang favored receiving surrendered rebels, and there was the upheaval of Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: I believe disaster often begins where caution is abandoned: the Western Han elevated imperial in-laws and brought on Wang Mang's usurpation; Emperor Wu of Liang welcomed defectors and triggered Hou Jing's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今者累歲北幸，狃于無虞，往而不止，臣甚懼焉。

translations.literal: Now, for successive years of northern visits, one has become accustomed to being without worry, going and not stopping—your subject is greatly afraid of this.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year of northern tours has bred complacency—the habit continues unchecked, and I am deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 夫事知其不可猶冒為之，則有後難必矣。

translations.literal: When one knows a matter cannot be done yet still rashly does it, later difficulty is inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: When one persists in what one knows to be unwise, disaster is sure to follow.

sentences.zh: 議者又謂往年遼國之君，春水秋山，冬夏捺缽，舊人猶喜談之，以為真得快樂之趣，陛下效之耳。

translations.literal: Those who debate further say that in former years the rulers of the Liao state had spring water and autumn mountains, winter and summer nabo camps; old people still delight in speaking of them, thinking they truly attained the pleasure of joy—Your Majesty is merely emulating them.
translations.idiomatic: Others cite the old Liao emperors' seasonal camps—spring waters, autumn mountains, summer and winter nabo—and say veterans still speak fondly of those pleasures, as though Your Majesty were simply following their example.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以謂三代之政今有不可行者，況遼之過舉哉。

translations.literal: Your subject foolishly holds that among the policies of the Three Dynasties there are some today that cannot be carried out—how much more so Liao's excessive actions?
translations.idiomatic: I would argue that even some policies of the Three Dynasties would be impracticable today—let alone the excesses of Liao.

sentences.zh: 且本朝與遼室異，遼之基業根本，在山北之臨潢，臣知其所遊，不過臨潢之旁，亦無重山之隔，冬猶處於燕京。

translations.literal: Moreover, this dynasty differs from the Liao house: Liao's foundation and root lay at Linhuang north of the mountains; your subject knows that where they traveled was no more than beside Linhuang, with no barrier of layered mountains, and in winter they still remained at Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty differs fundamentally from Liao: Liao's base lay at Linhuang north of the mountains, and their tours never went far from it, with no great mountain barrier—and even in winter they stayed at Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 契丹之人，以逐水草牧畜為業，穹廬為居，遷徙無常，又壤地褊小，儀物殊簡，輜重不多，然隔三五歲方能一行，非歲歲皆如此也。

translations.literal: The Khitan people took following water and grass to herd livestock as their occupation, yurts as their dwellings, and moved without fixed pattern; moreover their territory was narrow and small, ritual objects exceptionally simple, and baggage not abundant—yet only after three or five years could they make one journey; it was not every year that all was thus.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan lived as nomadic herders in yurts, roaming without fixed abode; their realm was small, their equipage simple, and their baggage light—yet even they made such journeys only every three to five years, not annually.

sentences.zh: 我本朝皇業，根本在山南之燕，豈可舍燕而之山北乎？

translations.literal: Our dynasty's imperial enterprise has its root in Yan south of the mountains—how can one abandon Yan and go to the north of the mountains?
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's foundation lies in Yan south of the mountains—how can we abandon Yan for the northern wastes?

sentences.zh: 上京之人，棟宇是居，不便遷徙。

translations.literal: The people of the Upper Capital dwell in houses and buildings and are not suited to relocation.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Upper Capital live in permanent houses and are ill suited to constant migration.

sentences.zh: 方今幅員萬里，惟奉一君，承平日久，制度殊異，文物增廣，輜重浩穰，隨駕生聚，殆逾于百萬。

translations.literal: At present the domain spans ten thousand li, all serving one ruler; peace has lasted long, institutions are entirely different, culture and objects have greatly expanded, baggage is vast and abundant, and the population following the imperial carriage probably exceeds a million.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm spans ten thousand li under a single sovereign; after long peace its institutions, culture, and material wealth have vastly expanded, and the retinue on tour may exceed a million souls.

sentences.zh: 如何歲歲而行，以一身之樂，歲使百萬之人困於役、傷於財、不得其所，陛下其忍之歟？

translations.literal: How can one travel year after year, for the pleasure of one person, year after year making a million people exhausted by corvée, harmed in wealth, and unable to find their proper place—can Your Majesty bear this?
translations.idiomatic: How can Your Majesty tour every year for personal pleasure, year after year imposing forced labor and financial ruin on a million people—can you truly countenance that?

sentences.zh: 臣又聞，陛下于合圍之際，麋鹿充牣圍中，大而壯者，才取數十以奉宗廟，餘皆縱之，不欲多殺。

translations.literal: Your subject has also heard that when Your Majesty closes the encircled hunt, elk and deer fill the enclosure; of the large and strong, only several tens are taken to serve the ancestral temple, and the rest are all released—unwilling to kill many.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that at the great encirclement hunt, when deer fill the ring, Your Majesty takes only a few dozen of the largest and strongest for the ancestral temple and releases the rest, unwilling to slaughter more.

sentences.zh: 是陛下恩及于禽獸，而未及於隨駕眾多之臣庶也。

translations.literal: This means Your Majesty's grace reaches birds and beasts, yet has not reached the many officials and commoners who follow the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's mercy extends even to game animals, yet not to the vast multitude of officials and commoners who follow the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 議者謂，前世守文之主，生長深宮。

translations.literal: Those who debate say that rulers of former ages who guarded culture grew up in deep palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Some argue that cultured rulers of old were raised in deep palace seclusion.

sentences.zh: 畏見風日，彎弧上馬，皆所不能，志氣銷懦，筋力拘柔，臨難戰懼，束手就亡。

translations.literal: They feared seeing wind and sun; drawing the bow and mounting the horse—they could do none of these; will and spirit wasted into timidity, sinew and strength constrained into softness; facing hardship they feared battle and, hands bound, met destruction.
translations.idiomatic: They shrank from wind and sunlight, could neither draw a bow nor mount a horse, grew timid and soft, and when crisis came they cowered helplessly to their doom.

sentences.zh: 陛下監其如此，不憚勤身，遠幸金蓮，至於松漠，名為坐夏打圍，實欲服勞講武。

translations.literal: Your Majesty observed that matters were thus, feared not to exert the person, traveled far to Jinlian, reaching Songmo—named as sitting out summer and conducting the encircled hunt, but in reality wishing to submit to labor and discuss martial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this danger, Your Majesty has not shunned personal hardship, touring as far as Jinlian and Songmo—nominally to escape the summer heat and hunt, but in truth to harden yourself through martial training.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為戰不可忘，畋獵不可廢，宴安鴆毒亦不可懷，然事貴適中，不可過當。

translations.literal: Your subject foolishly thinks that war cannot be forgotten, hunting cannot be abandoned, and the poison of feasting in ease cannot be cherished—yet matters value hitting the mean and cannot go beyond what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: I agree that warfare must not be forgotten, hunting should not be abandoned, and the seductive ease of the palace must be resisted—but all things require moderation, not excess.

sentences.zh: 今過防驕惰之患，先蹈萬有一危之途，何異無病而服藥也。

translations.literal: Now, in going beyond guarding against the harm of arrogance and indolence, one first treads a path of one-in-ten-thousand peril—how is this different from taking medicine when there is no illness?
translations.idiomatic: In guarding against the softness of palace life, you have embraced a path of needless peril—as though swallowing medicine when there is no sickness.

sentences.zh: 況欲習武不必度關，涿、易、雄、保、順、薊之境地廣又平，且在邦域之中，獵田以時，誰曰不可？

translations.literal: Moreover, if one wishes to practice martial affairs, there is no need to cross the passes; the territories of Zhuo, Yi, Xiong, Bao, Shun, and Ji are broad and level, and moreover lie within the domain—hunting fields at the proper season: who would say it cannot be done?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, martial training need not cross the frontier passes—the broad flat lands of Zhuo, Yi, Xiong, Bao, Shun, and Ji lie well within the realm; seasonal hunting there would serve the same purpose. Who could object?

sentences.zh: 伏乞陛下發如綸之旨，回北轅之車，塞雞鳴之路，安處中都，不復北幸，則宗社無疆之休，天下莫大之願也。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly begs Your Majesty to issue an edict like silken cords, turn back the northern axle of the carriage, block the road of the cock's crow, dwell securely at the Central Capital, and no longer make northern visits—then the boundless blessing of the ancestral temple and state, and the greatest wish of all under Heaven, would be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to issue a solemn decree, turn the imperial carriage south, close the northern road, and remain securely at the Central Capital without further northern tours—the boundless blessing of the dynasty and the deepest wish of the realm would then be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 方今海內安治，朝廷尊嚴，聖人作事，固臣下將順之時，而臣以螻蟻之命，進危切之言，仰犯雷霆之威，陷於吏議，小則名位削除，大則身首分磔，其為身計，豈不愚謬。

translations.literal: At present within the seas there is peace and good order, the court is dignified, and when the sage acts, it is naturally the time for ministers to comply and follow—yet your subject, with the life of an ant, advances words of peril and urgency, looking up to offend the thunderbolt's majesty, falling into official censure; in small matters name and rank may be stripped, in great matters body and head may be quartered—for one's own person, is this not foolish and absurd?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is at peace and the court commands dignity; this is a time when ministers should comply, not remonstrate. Yet I, a man of no account, speak words of grave warning, risking imperial wrath and official punishment—from loss of rank to execution by dismemberment. By any measure of self-preservation, I must seem a fool.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下深思博慮，不以人廢言，以宗廟天下為心，俯垂聽納，則小臣素願遂獲，雖死猶生，他非所覬望也。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty deeply thinks and broadly considers, does not reject words because of the person, takes the ancestral temple and all under Heaven to heart, and bends down to listen and accept—then your subject's long-held wish will be fulfilled; though dead, it would be as living; other things are not what he hopes for.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty reflects deeply, judges the message rather than the messenger, and keeps the dynasty and the realm at heart will my lifelong wish be granted—I would count even death as life itself, and ask for nothing more.

sentences.zh: 世宗納之，遂為罷行，仍諭輔臣曰：「梁襄諫朕毋幸金蓮川，朕以其言可取，故罷其行。

translations.literal: Shizong accepted it and thereupon canceled the journey; he still instructed the chief ministers, saying, "Liang Xiang remonstrated that I should not visit Jinlian River; I took his words as acceptable, and therefore canceled the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong accepted the memorial and canceled the tour, then told his chief ministers, "Liang Xiang urged me not to visit Jinlian River; I found his argument persuasive and called off the journey.

sentences.zh: 然襄至謂隋煬帝以巡遊敗國，不亦過乎。

translations.literal: Yet for Xiang to go so far as to say that Sui Yangdi ruined the state through touring— is that not excessive?
translations.idiomatic: But for Xiang to claim that Sui Yangdi destroyed his dynasty through touring alone—that goes too far, does it not?

sentences.zh: 如煬帝者蓋由失道虐民，自取滅亡。

translations.literal: One such as Yangdi was essentially because he lost the Way and tyrannized the people, bringing destruction upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler like Yangdi perished because he abandoned the Way and oppressed his people—he brought ruin upon himself.

sentences.zh: 民心既叛，雖不巡幸，國將安保？

translations.literal: Once the people's hearts have turned in rebellion, even without touring, how would the state be kept secure?
translations.idiomatic: Once the people had turned against him, how could the state have survived even if he had never toured?

sentences.zh: 為人上者，但能盡君道，則雖時或巡幸，庸何傷乎？

translations.literal: For one who stands above others, if one can only fully fulfill the way of a ruler, then even if one occasionally tours, what harm would there be?
translations.idiomatic: If a sovereign truly fulfills his duties, what harm could occasional tours possibly do?

sentences.zh: 治亂無常，顧所行何如耳。

translations.literal: Order and disorder have no fixed pattern—it depends only on how one acts.
translations.idiomatic: Peace and chaos follow no fixed rule; everything depends on how a ruler governs.

sentences.zh: 豈必深處九重便謂無虞，巡遊以時即兆禍亂者哉！」

translations.literal: Must one deep within the ninefold palace then say there is no worry, and that touring at the proper season is the omen of calamity and disorder?"
translations.idiomatic: Must one believe that dwelling deep in the palace guarantees safety, while timely tours inevitably foretell disaster?"

sentences.zh: 襄由是以直聲聞。

translations.literal: Xiang thereby became known for his upright reputation.
translations.idiomatic: From this Xiang earned a reputation for fearless integrity.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部主事、太子司經。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Clerk of the Ministry of Rites and Instructor in the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to clerk in the Ministry of Rites and instructor in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 選為監察御史，坐失察宗室弈事，罰俸一月。

translations.literal: He was selected as Investigating Censor; for failing to detect a chess affair among the imperial clan, his salary was fined for one month.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor but was fined one month's salary for failing to uncover a gambling scandal among imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 世宗責之曰：「監察，人君耳目，風聲彈事可也。

translations.literal: Shizong rebuked him, saying, "Investigating censors are the ruler's eyes and ears; reporting on rumors and impeaching matters is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong rebuked him: "Censors are the emperor's eyes and ears—it is their duty to investigate rumors and lodge impeachments.

sentences.zh: 至朕親發其事，何以監察為？

translations.literal: But when it reaches the point that I personally expose the matter, what use is there in being an investigating censor?
translations.idiomatic: But when the emperor must uncover the affair himself, of what use are censors at all?

sentences.zh: 」轉中都路都轉運戶籍判官，未幾，遷通遠軍節度副使，以喪去。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Household Register Judge of the Central Capital Circuit Transport Commission; before long he was promoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Tongyuan Army and left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " He became Household Register Judge on the Central Capital transport commission, was soon promoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Tongyuan Army, and left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 服闋，授安國軍節度副使，同知定武軍節度事，避父諱改震武軍。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended he was appointed Vice Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army and Associate Administrator of the Dingwu Army; to avoid his father's taboo name he was changed to the Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Vice Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army with a concurrent post in the Dingwu Army; to avoid his father's taboo name the assignment was changed to the Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 太常卿張暐、曹州刺史段鐸薦襄學問該博，練習典故，可任禮官。

translations.literal: Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhang Wei and Prefect of Caozhou Duan Duo recommended Xiang as learned and comprehensive, practiced in precedents, and fit to serve as a ritual official.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Duan Duo, prefect of Caozhou, recommended Xiang as broadly learned and versed in ritual precedent, fit for a post in the ritual offices.

sentences.zh: 轉同知順義軍節度使事、東勝州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Associate Administrator of the Shunyi Army and Prefect of Dongshengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as Associate Administrator of the Shunyi Army and prefect of Dongshengzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐簸揚俸粟責倉典使償，為按察司所劾，以贖論。

translations.literal: He was punished for winnowing and scattering salary grain and ordering the granary clerk to make restitution; the surveillance commission impeached him, and he was sentenced by ransom.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for mishandling salary grain and making the granary clerk pay restitution. The surveillance commission impeached him, and he was allowed to redeem the offense.

sentences.zh: 曆隩州刺史，累遷保大軍節度使，卒。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Youzhou, was repeatedly promoted to Military Commissioner of the Baoda Army, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Youzhou, rose through promotions to Military Commissioner of the Baoda Army, and died.

sentences.zh: 襄長於《春秋左氏傳》，至於地理、氏族，無不該貫。

translations.literal: Xiang excelled in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; as for geography and clans, there was nothing he did not master comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was expert in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and thoroughly versed in geography and clan genealogy.

sentences.zh: 自蚤達至晚貴，膳服常淡薄，然議者譏其太儉雲。

translations.literal: From early advancement to late eminence, his food and dress were always plain and thin, yet critics mocked him as too frugal.
translations.idiomatic: From his early rise to his late eminence, his food and clothing remained plain, though some criticized him as excessively austere.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金起東海，始立國即設科取士，蓋亦知有文治也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Jin arose from the Eastern Sea; at the very founding of the state it established examinations to select scholars—surely it also knew there was civil governance.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: The Jin arose from the Eastern Sea. From the founding of the state it established examinations to select scholars, showing that it understood the value of civil governance.

sentences.zh: 漸摩培養，至大定間人材輩出，文義蔚然。

translations.literal: Through gradual cultivation and nurturing, by the Dading era talents emerged in succession and literary culture flourished luxuriantly.
translations.idiomatic: Through gradual cultivation, by the Dading era talents emerged in succession and literary culture flourished.

sentences.zh: 加以世宗之聽納，人各盡其所能，論議書疏有可傳者。

translations.literal: Added to this was Shizong's willingness to listen and accept; each man exhausted what he could do, and in discussion, memorials, and letters there were works worth transmitting.
translations.idiomatic: With Shizong's willingness to listen and accept counsel, men gave their best, and many memorials and essays from that age are worth preserving.

sentences.zh: 惜史無全文，僅存梁襄《諫北幸》一書，辭雖過繁而意亦切至，故備載之，以見當時君明臣直，不以言為忌。

translations.literal: It is a pity the histories lack full texts; only Liang Xiang's book "Remonstrance Against the Northern Tour" survives. Though the language is overly elaborate, the intent is also earnest and penetrating; therefore it is recorded in full, to show that at the time the ruler was enlightened and the ministers upright, and speech was not treated as taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Regrettably the histories preserve few full texts; only Liang Xiang's "Remonstrance Against the Northern Tour" survives. Though verbose, its intent is earnest, and it is recorded here to show an age when the ruler was enlightened, ministers were upright, and frank speech was not feared.

sentences.zh: 金之致治于斯為盛，嗚呼休哉。

translations.literal: Jin's attainment of good order reached its height at this point—alas, how excellent!
translations.idiomatic: The Jin reached the height of good government in this age—how excellent indeed!

sentences.zh: 路伯達

translations.literal: Lu Boda
translations.idiomatic: Lu Boda

sentences.zh: 路伯達，字仲顯，冀州人也。

translations.literal: Lu Boda, styled Zhongxian, was a man of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Boda, whose courtesy name was Zhongxian, came from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 性沉厚，有遠識，博學能詩，登正隆五年進士第，調諸城主簿。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and steady, with far-reaching discernment; broadly learned and able in poetry, he attained jinshi rank in the fifth year of Zhenglong and was appointed chief clerk of Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and steady by nature, with far-sighted judgment, he was broadly learned and wrote poetry well. He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Zhenglong and was posted as chief clerk in Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 由泗州榷場使補尚書省掾，除興平軍節度副使，入為大理司直。

translations.literal: From commissioner of the Sizhou monopoly market he was appointed clerk in the Ministry of Works, was made Vice Military Commissioner of the Xingping Army, and entered service as Directing Officer in the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: From commissioner of the Sizhou monopoly market he became a clerk in the Ministry of Works, was appointed Vice Military Commissioner of the Xingping Army, and entered the Court of Review as Directing Officer.

sentences.zh: 大定二十四年，世宗將幸上京，伯達上書諫曰：「人君以四海為家，豈獨舊邦是思，空京師而事遠巡，非重慎之道也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Dading, when Shizong was about to visit the Upper Capital, Boda submitted a written remonstrance, saying, "The ruler takes the four seas as his home—how should he think only of the old domain? To empty the capital and attend to distant tours is not the way of grave caution.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Dading, as Shizong prepared to visit the Upper Capital, Boda submitted a written remonstrance: "A ruler takes the four seas as his home. Why think only of the old domain? To empty the capital for distant tours is not the way of prudent rule.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，不報。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 閱歲，改秘書郎，兼太子司經。

translations.literal: After a year he was changed to Secretary and concurrently Master of Classics for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed Secretary with a concurrent post as Master of Classics for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時章宗初向學，伯達以文行知名，選為侍讀，居無何以憂去。

translations.literal: At the time Zhangzong was first turning to study; Boda was renowned for literary conduct and was selected as Lecturer-in-Attendance, but before long he left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong was then beginning his studies. Boda, renowned for learning and conduct, was selected as Lecturer-in-Attendance but soon left office to mourn.

sentences.zh: 會安武軍節度使王克溫舉伯達行義，起為同知西京路轉運使事，召為尚書禮部員外郎，兼翰林修撰，敕與張行簡進讀陳言文字。

translations.literal: It happened that Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army Wang Kewen recommended Boda for moral conduct; he was recalled to serve as Associate Administrator of the Western Capital Circuit Transport Commission, was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Ministry of Works, concurrently Hanlin Compiler, and ordered with Zhang Xingjian to read submitted memorials aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kewen, Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army, recommended Boda for moral integrity. Recalled from mourning, he became Associate Administrator of the Western Capital transport commission, was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites with a concurrent Hanlin Compiler post, and was ordered with Zhang Xingjian to read submitted memorials aloud.

sentences.zh: 先是，右丞相襄奏移賀天壽節於九月一日，伯達論列以其非時，平章政事張汝霖、右丞劉瑋及台諫亦皆言其不可，下尚書省議，伯達曰：「上始即政，當行正、信之道，今易生辰非正，以紿四方非信。

translations.literal: Earlier, Right Chancellor Xiang memorialized to move the celebration of the Heavenly Longevity Festival to the first day of the ninth month. Boda argued in array that the timing was wrong; Grand Councillor Zhang Rulin, Vice Director Liu Wei, and the censorial and remonstrance offices all also said it could not be done. The matter was sent down to the Ministry of Works for deliberation. Boda said, "Your Majesty has just taken the throne and ought to practice the ways of rectitude and trustworthiness. Now to change the birthday is not rectitude; to deceive the four quarters is not trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Right Chancellor Xiang had proposed moving the Heavenly Longevity Festival celebration to the first day of the ninth month. Boda argued the timing was improper; Grand Councillor Zhang Rulin, Vice Director Liu Wei, and the censorial and remonstrance offices agreed. When the matter was referred to the Ministry of Works, Boda said, "Your Majesty has just ascended the throne and should uphold rectitude and trust. Changing the birthday date is not rectitude; deceiving the realm is not trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 且賀非其時，是輕禮重物也。

translations.literal: Moreover, to congratulate at the wrong time is to slight ritual and esteem material things.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, celebrating at the wrong season slighted ritual in favor of material convenience.

sentences.zh: 」因陳正名從諫之道。

translations.literal: " He then set forth the way of rectifying names and following remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: " He then expounded the principles of rectifying names and heeding remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 升尚書刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Punishments of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 上問群臣曰：「方今何道使民務本業、廣儲蓄？

translations.literal: The emperor asked the assembled ministers, "By what way today can the people be made to attend to their basic occupations and broaden storage?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers, "What policy today will make the people attend to basic production and build up reserves?

sentences.zh: 」伯達對曰：「布德流化，必自近始。

translations.literal: " Boda replied, "Spreading virtue and diffusing transformation must begin with what is near.
translations.idiomatic: " Boda answered, "Spreading virtue and transforming customs must begin close at hand.

sentences.zh: 請罷畿內采獵之禁，廣農郊以示敦本，輕幣重穀，去奢長儉，遵月令開籍田以率先天下，如是而農不勸、粟不廣者未之有也。

translations.literal: I beg to abolish the prohibition on hunting within the capital region, expand the agricultural suburbs to show esteem for the root, make light of goods and esteem grain, remove extravagance and extend frugality, follow the monthly ordinances and open the ceremonial field to take the lead for all under Heaven—if it is thus, there has never been a case where agriculture was not encouraged and grain not broadened.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish the hunting ban in the capital region, expand suburban farming to show devotion to fundamentals, value grain over luxury goods, curb extravagance and promote thrift, and open the ceremonial field according to seasonal ordinance to lead the realm by example. Then agriculture will surely flourish and stores will grow.

sentences.zh: 」是時，採捕禁嚴，自京畿至真定、滄、冀，北及飛狐，數百里內皆為禁地，民有盜殺狐兔者有罪，故伯達及之。

translations.literal: " At the time the prohibition on gathering and hunting was severe; from the capital region to Zhending, Cang, and Ji, north to Feihu, within several hundred li all was forbidden ground—commoners who secretly killed foxes or hares were guilty; therefore Boda touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: " Hunting and gathering were then strictly forbidden from the capital region through Zhending, Cang, and Ji north to Feihu—hundreds of li of forbidden ground where killing even foxes or hares was a crime. That is why Boda raised the issue.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部侍郎、太常卿，拜安國軍節度使，未幾，改鎮安武。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Vice Minister of Punishments and Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was appointed Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army, and before long was transferred to command Anwu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Vice Minister of Punishments and Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was appointed Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army, and soon transferred to command Anwu.

sentences.zh: 嘗使宋回，獻所得金二百五十兩、銀一千兩以助邊，表乞致仕，未及上而卒。

translations.literal: Once, on returning from an embassy to the Song, he presented the gold of two hundred fifty taels and silver of one thousand taels he had received to assist the frontier; he submitted a memorial begging to retire from office, but before it could be submitted he died.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from a mission to the Song he presented 250 taels of gold and 1,000 taels of silver he had received to support the frontier, and drafted a retirement memorial, but died before it could be submitted.

sentences.zh: 其妻傅氏言之，上嘉其誠，贈太中大夫，仍以金銀還之，傅泣請，弗許。

translations.literal: His wife, the Fu clan, reported this; the emperor praised his sincerity, posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace, and still returned the gold and silver—Fu wept and begged, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Fu reported this. The emperor praised his sincerity, posthumously granted him Grand Master of the Palace, and ordered the gold and silver returned. Lady Fu wept and begged to keep them, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 傅以伯達嘗修冀州學，乃市信都、棗強田以贍學，有司具以聞，上賢之，賜號成德夫人。

translations.literal: Fu, because Boda had once restored the Jizhou school, then purchased fields in Xindu and Zaoqiang to support the school; the responsible offices reported this in full; the emperor deemed her worthy and granted the title Lady of Accomplished Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Because Boda had once restored the school in Jizhou, Lady Fu used the returned funds to buy fields in Xindu and Zaoqiang to support it. When officials reported this, the emperor praised her and granted the title Lady of Accomplished Virtue.

sentences.zh: 子鐸、鈞。

translations.literal: Sons: Duo and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Duo and Jun.

sentences.zh: 鈞字和叔，登大定二十五年進士第，終萊州觀察判官。

translations.literal: Jun, styled Heshu, attained jinshi rank in the twenty-fifth year of Dading and ended as surveillance judge of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, courtesy name Heshu, passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Dading and ended his career as surveillance judge in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 鐸最知名，別有傳。

translations.literal: Duo was most renowned and has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was the most famous and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金詘宋稱臣稱侄，受其歲幣，禮也。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Jin humbled Song into calling itself subject and nephew and received its annual tribute—this was ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: The Jin humbled the Song into acknowledging subject and nephew status and received annual tribute—this was ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 使聘于其國，燕享禮也，納其重賂其可乎哉？

translations.literal: To send envoys to their state and receive them with banquet and feast is ritual propriety—but to accept their heavy bribes, how can that be permissible?
translations.idiomatic: Sending envoys and receiving them with proper banquet ritual was correct—but accepting heavy bribes from them, how could that be right?

sentences.zh: 時人貪利忘禮，習以為常，莫有知其為非者。

translations.literal: Men of the time, greedy for profit, forgot ritual propriety; they took it as custom, and none knew it was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time were greedy for profit and forgot ritual propriety. The practice had become custom, and scarcely anyone recognized it as wrong.

sentences.zh: 故去則雲酬勞效，還則戶增物力，上下交征，惟利是事，此何誼耶？

translations.literal: Therefore on departure they would say it was reward for labor and service; on return households would increase material goods—superiors and subordinates mutually exacting, serving only profit. What propriety is this?
translations.idiomatic: On departure they called it reward for service; on return households grew richer—superiors and subordinates alike pursuing profit alone. What sense of propriety was this?

sentences.zh: 伯達獨能明其非禮，回獻所饋，齎志未畢，傅氏又能成之，及歸所獻，竟以買田贍學。

translations.literal: Boda alone could clarify that it was not ritual propriety; on his return he presented what had been given, carrying his intent unfinished; the Fu clan was able to complete it, and when the presented gifts were returned, in the end they were used to buy fields to support the school.
translations.idiomatic: Boda alone recognized the impropriety and, on his return, presented the gifts he had received. He died before his intent was fulfilled, but Lady Fu completed it: when the court returned the gold and silver, she used them to buy fields to support the school.

sentences.zh: 婦人秉心之烈、制事之宜，乃能如是，士大夫溺于世俗之見者寧不愧哉。

translations.literal: A woman holding fierce resolution in her heart and fitness in ordering affairs could act thus—should scholar-officials drowned in worldly views not feel ashamed?
translations.idiomatic: That a woman of such fierce integrity and sound judgment could act thus—should scholar-officials drowned in worldly convention not feel ashamed?

sentences.zh: 賜號成德，不亦宜乎。

translations.literal: To grant the title Accomplished Virtue—is it not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: The title Lady of Accomplished Virtue was richly deserved.
